short_description.id: Qianlima adalah kuda luar biasa yang dikatakan dapat menempuh seribu li dalam sehari.
short_description.en: Qianlima is an exceptional horse said to travel a thousand li in one day.

long_description.id: Qianlima adalah kuda luar biasa yang dikatakan dapat menempuh seribu li dalam sehari. Nama kuda ini muncul dalam teks klasik seperti Chu Ci dan Records of the Grand Historian. Bole digambarkan mampu mengenali kuda dengan kemampuan istimewa ini.
long_description.en: Qianlima is an exceptional horse said to travel a thousand li in one day. The horse appears in classical texts such as the Chu Ci and Records of the Grand Historian. Bole is portrayed as able to recognise horses with this exceptional ability.

long_description.id: Teks Ma Shuo menekankan bahwa kuda seribu li membutuhkan makanan sangat banyak, sehingga kemampuannya hilang bila pemeliharanya tidak memahaminya. Dalam Zhanguo Ce, Guo Wei menceritakan raja yang gagal mencari kuda seribu li selama tiga tahun, lalu pelayannya membeli kepala kuda yang sudah mati seharga lima ratus keping emas; dalam setahun tiga kuda seribu li datang.
long_description.en: The Ma Shuo stresses that a thousand-li horse needs a great deal of food, so its ability is lost when its keeper does not understand it. In the Zhanguo Ce, Guo Wei tells of a ruler who failed to find a thousand-li horse for three years until his attendant bought the head of a dead one for five hundred pieces of gold; within a year three thousand-li horses arrived.

long_description.id: Sebuah kajian yang dirujuk Wikipedia memperkirakan satu li kuno sekitar 600 meter, sehingga jarak seribu li sehari dianggap tidak mustahil.
long_description.en: A study cited by Wikipedia estimates an ancient li at about 600 metres, so a thousand li a day is considered not impossible.

statement.id: Menurut sebuah kajian yang dirujuk Wikipedia, satu li zaman dahulu kira-kira 600 meter, sehingga "seribu li sehari" hanya sekitar 600 kilometer per hari dan bukan hal yang mustahil.
statement.en: According to a study cited by Wikipedia, an ancient li was about 600 metres, so "a thousand li a day" is only about 600 kilometres per day and not impossible.

claims.quote: 馬之千里者，一食或盡粟一石。食馬者，不知其能千里而食也。是馬也，雖有千里之能，食不飽，力不足

statement.id: Dalam teks Ma Shuo (馬說), kuda seribu li kadang menghabiskan satu dan biji-bijian sekali makan; pemberi makan yang tidak tahu kemampuannya tidak memberinya cukup, sehingga meski mampu menempuh seribu li, ia lapar dan kurang tenaga.
statement.en: In the Ma Shuo (馬說), a thousand-li horse may finish a dan of grain at one meal; a keeper who does not know its ability fails to feed it enough, so although capable of a thousand li, it goes hungry and lacks strength.

claims.quote: 郭隗先生曰：「臣聞古之君人，有以千金求千里馬者，三年不能得。

statement.id: Dalam Zhanguo Ce (戰國策), Guo Wei (郭隗) menceritakan seorang raja zaman dahulu yang mencari kuda seribu li dengan seribu keping emas tetapi selama tiga tahun tidak mendapatkannya.
statement.en: In the Zhanguo Ce (戰國策), Guo Wei (郭隗) tells of a ruler of old who sought a thousand-li horse for a thousand pieces of gold but failed to obtain one for three years.

claims.quote: 言於君曰：『請求之。』君遣之。三月得千里馬，馬已死，買其首五百金，反以報君。

statement.id: Seorang pelayan istana menawarkan diri mencarinya; dalam tiga bulan ia menemukan kuda seribu li yang sudah mati, membeli kepalanya seharga lima ratus keping emas, lalu kembali melapor.
statement.en: A palace attendant offered to search; within three months he found a thousand-li horse that had already died, bought its head for five hundred pieces of gold and returned to report.

claims.quote: 『死馬且買之五百金，況生馬乎？天下必以王為能市馬，馬今至矣。』於是不能期年，千里之馬至者三。

statement.id: Pelayan itu beralasan bahwa jika kuda mati saja dibeli lima ratus keping emas, orang akan yakin raja sungguh mau membeli kuda; dalam kurang dari setahun, tiga kuda seribu li pun datang.
statement.en: The attendant reasoned that if even a dead horse fetched five hundred pieces of gold, the world would believe the king truly bought horses; within less than a year three thousand-li horses arrived.

short_description.id: Tahoe Tessie adalah kriptid yang konon menghuni kedalaman Lake Tahoe di perbatasan California dan Nevada [tahoe-tessie-c01].
short_description.en: Tahoe Tessie is a cryptid believed to live deep in Lake Tahoe, on the California–Nevada border [tahoe-tessie-c01].

long_description.id: Tahoe Tessie adalah kriptid yang konon menghuni kedalaman Lake Tahoe [tahoe-tessie-c01]. Laporannya sudah ada sejak pertengahan abad ke-19 [tahoe-tessie-c02]; salah satu yang paling awal berasal dari I.C. Coggin pada tahun 1865 [tahoe-tessie-c03].
long_description.en: Tahoe Tessie is a cryptid believed to live deep in Lake Tahoe [tahoe-tessie-c01]. Reports go back to the mid-19th century [tahoe-tessie-c02]; one of the earliest came from I.C. Coggin in 1865 [tahoe-tessie-c03].

long_description.id: Legendanya sering dikaitkan dengan kepercayaan Washoe tentang Water Babies [tahoe-tessie-c04], meski bentuknya saat ini terutama berasal dari abad ke-20 [tahoe-tessie-c05] dan sering dibandingkan dengan Nessie [tahoe-tessie-c06]. Ada teori bahwa makhluk itu ikan sturgeon raksasa [tahoe-tessie-c07], sementara Charles Goldman menjelaskan banyak penampakan sebagai efek angin atau gerakan air [tahoe-tessie-c08].
long_description.en: The legend is often linked to Washoe beliefs in Water Babies [tahoe-tessie-c04], though its current form dates mainly to the 20th century [tahoe-tessie-c05] and is often compared to Nessie [tahoe-tessie-c06]. One theory holds it is a giant sturgeon [tahoe-tessie-c07], while Charles Goldman attributes many sightings to wind or water movements [tahoe-tessie-c08].

long_description.id: Menurut Moonshine Ink, cerita tentang monster di Tahoe sudah ada sekitar 100 tahun dan penampakannya dilaporkan sejak awal abad ke-20, sementara nama Tahoe Tessie sendiri jauh lebih muda. Bob McCormick, warga Kings Beach, mengaku menciptakan nama itu saat berkayak bersama temannya pada 1975 dan menerbitkan buku bergambar tentang Tessie pada 1984. Dalam wujud modernnya Tessie dikatakan mirip dinosaurus, kemungkinan karena pengaruh Nessie dari Loch Ness.
long_description.en: According to Moonshine Ink, stories of a Tahoe monster go back about 100 years and sightings have been reported since the early 20th century, while the name Tahoe Tessie itself is much younger. Kings Beach resident Bob McCormick says he dreamed up the name on a kayaking trip with a friend in 1975 and published an illustrated book about Tessie in 1984. In her modern form Tessie is said to resemble a dinosaur, perhaps under the influence of Nessie of Loch Ness.

long_description.id: Laporan penampakan biasanya menggambarkan bentuk gelap berpunuk di permukaan air; dalam satu kesaksian, bentuk itu tampak padat dengan tiga sampai lima punuk di punggungnya. Goldman mencatat bahwa para saksi tidak pernah melaporkan kepala atau ekor, hanya bentuk gelap di dalam air.
long_description.en: Sighting reports usually describe a dark, humped shape at the surface; in one account it looked solid, with three to five humps along its back. Goldman observed that witnesses never report a head or a tail, just dark shapes in the water.

claims.quote: Tahoe Tessie is a cryptid said to inhabit the depths of Lake Tahoe, a lake that straddles the border between California and Nevada.

claims.quote: Although some claim that Tessie has roots in Washoe culture, the current form of the legend dates primarily to the 20th century.

long_description.en: Quru is a bird with a human face recorded in the Shan Hai Jing. It has a white head and three feet.

long_description.id: Suaranya disebut menyerukan namanya sendiri. Bagian selatan Shan Hai Jing menempatkan Quru pada Gunung Daoguo. Teks yang disertai komentar membandingkan bentuk Quru dengan burung Jiao.
long_description.en: Its voice is said to call its own name. The southern section of the Shan Hai Jing places Quru on Mount Daoguo. The text with commentary compares Quru's form with the Jiao bird.

long_description.id: Teks primer Shanhaijing bagian Selatan menempatkan burung ini di gunung 禱過之山: bentuknya seperti 鵁, kepala putih, berkaki tiga, berwajah manusia, dan bunyinya menyebut namanya sendiri. Catatan pada teks itu menyebut 鵁 mirip bebek tetapi lebih kecil dengan kaki dekat ekor, dan satu naskah memakai aksara 手 untuk 首 (kepala).
long_description.en: The primary text of the Southern section of the Shanhaijing places this bird on Mount 禱過之山: shaped like a 鵁, with a white head, three feet and a human face, and a cry that calls its own name. An annotation says the 鵁 resembles a duck but is smaller, with its legs near the tail, and one version writes 手 for 首 (head).

long_description.id: Gunung Daoguo digambarkan kaya emas dan giok di bagian atas, serta badak, si, dan gajah di bagian bawah. Guo Pu menjelaskan bahwa burung jiao mirip bebek liar, dan mencatat versi yang menulis tiga tangan alih-alih tiga kaki. Tuzan juga menyebut Quru bertangan tiga.
long_description.en: Mount Daoguo is described as rich in gold and jade on its upper slopes, with rhinoceroses, si and elephants below. Guo Pu explains that the jiao bird resembles a wild duck, and notes a version that writes three hands instead of three feet. The Tuzan also gives Quru three hands.

claims.quote: 瞿如，古譚異獸也，據《山海經》：「東五百里，曰禱過之山，其上多金玉，其下多犀、兕，多象。有鳥焉，其狀如鵁而白首，三足，人面，其名曰瞿如，其鳴自號也。」

claims.quote: 瞿如，古譚異獸也，據《山海經》：「東五百里，曰禱過之山，其上多金玉，其下多犀、兕，多象。有鳥焉，其狀如鵁而白首，三足，人面，其名曰瞿如，其鳴自號也。」

statement.id: Teks yang disertai komentar membandingkan bentuk Quru dengan burung Jiao.
statement.en: The text with commentary compares Quru's form with the Jiao bird.

claims.quote: 有鳥焉，其狀如鵁〈鵁似鳧而小腳近尾。音骹箭之骹〉，而白 首一作「手」、三足、人面，其名曰瞿如〈音劬〉，其鳴自號也。

statement.id: Teks Shanhaijing bagian Selatan menyebut di gunung 禱過之山 ada burung berbentuk seperti 鵁 dengan kepala putih (satu naskah memakai aksara 手 untuk 首), berkaki tiga, berwajah manusia, bernama 瞿如, dan berbunyi menyebut namanya sendiri; catatan menyebut 鵁 mirip bebek tetapi lebih kecil dengan kaki dekat ekor.
statement.en: The Southern section of the Shanhaijing says that on Mount 禱過之山 there is a bird shaped like a 鵁 with a white head (one version writes 手 for 首), three feet and a human face, named 瞿如, whose cry calls its own name; an annotation says the 鵁 resembles a duck but is smaller, with its legs near the tail.

claims.quote: 有鳥焉其狀如鵁〈郭曰鵁似鳬而小脚近尾音骹箭之骹〉而白首三足〈郭曰或作手〉人面其名曰瞿如
claims.locator: 南次三經, 禱過之山 (注)

statement.id: Catatan Guo Pu (郭) dalam Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注) menjelaskan bahwa burung jiao (鵁) mirip bebek liar (鳬) dengan kaki kecil di dekat ekor, dan bahwa "tiga kaki" Quru dalam versi lain ditulis "tangan" (手).
statement.en: Guo Pu's note (郭) in the Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注) explains that the jiao bird (鵁) resembles a wild duck (鳬) with small feet near the tail, and that Quru's "three feet" is written "hands" (手) in another version.

claims.quote: 皆龍種而蛟𩔖也〉其狀魚身而蛇尾其音如鴛鴦食者不腫可以已痔〈任臣案拾遺記漢昭帝釣于渭水得白蛟命大官作鮓甚美骨青而肉紫則蛟可食也圖贊曰瞿如三手厥狀似鵁魚身蛇尾是謂虎蛟〉
claims.locator: 南次三經, 禱過之山 (注)

statement.id: Tuzan (圖贊) yang dikutip di sana menyebut Quru bertangan tiga dan berwujud seperti burung jiao; bait yang sama menyebut makhluk berbadan ikan dan berekor ular sebagai Hujiao (虎蛟).
statement.en: The Tuzan (圖贊) quoted there says Quru has three hands and looks like a jiao bird; the same verse names the fish-bodied, snake-tailed creature Hujiao (虎蛟).

claims.quote: 「东五百里，曰祷过之山，其上多金玉，其下多犀、兕，多象。有鸟焉，其状如鵁而白首，三足，人面，其名曰瞿如，其鸣自号也。」

statement.id: Wikipedia mengutip teks bahwa Gunung Daoguo (祷过之山) kaya emas dan giok di atas, serta badak, si (兕), dan gajah di bawahnya, tempat burung Quru hidup.
statement.en: Wikipedia quotes the text: Mount Daoguo (祷过之山) has much gold and jade above, and rhinoceroses, si (兕) and elephants below, and is where the Quru bird lives.

short_description.id: Sirena Chilota adalah makhluk air setengah ikan setengah manusia dalam mitologi Chilote, putri bungsu Millalobo sang raja laut [sirena-chilota-c01, sirena-chilota-c03, sirena-chilota-c04].
short_description.en: The Sirena Chilota is a half-fish, half-human aquatic being of Chilote mythology, youngest daughter of Millalobo, king of the sea [sirena-chilota-c01, sirena-chilota-c03, sirena-chilota-c04].

long_description.id: Sirena Chilota adalah makhluk air dalam mitologi Chilote [sirena-chilota-c01] yang mungkin berasal dari perpaduan Sumpall Mapuche dan putri duyung Eropa [sirena-chilota-c02]. Ia setengah ikan setengah manusia, berambut pirang panjang, dan bersisik emas [sirena-chilota-c03], serta tinggal di dekat Pulau Laitec di Kepulauan Chiloé [sirena-chilota-c07].
long_description.en: The Sirena Chilota is an aquatic being of Chilote mythology [sirena-chilota-c01] that may combine the Mapuche Sumpall and the European mermaid [sirena-chilota-c02]. Part human and part fish, she has golden scales and long blonde hair [sirena-chilota-c03], and lives near the island of Laitec in the Chiloé Archipelago [sirena-chilota-c07].

long_description.id: Ia putri bungsu Millalobo dan Huenchula [sirena-chilota-c04], bertugas menggembalakan ikan [sirena-chilota-c05], dan membantu Pincoya dan Pincoy membawa pelaut yang tenggelam ke Caleuche [sirena-chilota-c06]. Ia dapat menggiring ikan ke perahu pelaut yang disukainya [sirena-chilota-c08], tetapi lagu cintanya memikat pria [sirena-chilota-c09] yang lalu dibawanya ke istana di dasar laut [sirena-chilota-c10].
long_description.en: She is the youngest daughter of Millalobo and Huenchula [sirena-chilota-c04], tasked with shepherding fish [sirena-chilota-c05], and helps the Pincoya and Pincoy carry drowned sailors to the Caleuche [sirena-chilota-c06]. She may drive fish to the boats of sailors she likes [sirena-chilota-c08], but her love songs lure men [sirena-chilota-c09] whom she takes to a palace at the bottom of the ocean [sirena-chilota-c10].

long_description.id: Bagian manusianya digambarkan sebagai remaja putri yang sangat cantik dengan rambut panjang keemasan. Pada malam berbulan, pelaut yang beruntung konon bisa melihatnya duduk di atas karang sambil menyisir rambut dengan sisir emas. Bila pria yang terpikat mencoba menjauh, ia akan menangis dan menceritakan kisah kesepiannya sampai pria itu luluh. Pria yang dibawanya ke bawah air tidak bisa kembali ke kehidupan lamanya di darat, tetapi menerima kekayaan yang sangat besar sebagai gantinya. Menurut legenda, keturunan pria yang pernah bersamanya kelak lahir dengan ekor ikan.
long_description.en: Her human half is described as a very beautiful adolescent girl with long golden hair. On moonlit nights a lucky sailor may see her sitting on the rocks, combing her hair with a golden comb. If a captivated man tries to leave, she weeps and tells her story of loneliness until he gives in. A man she takes beneath the water cannot return to his former life on land, but receives immense riches in exchange. According to legend, the later descendants of a man who slept with her are born with fish tails.

short_description.en: Jiaoren are merperson like beings in Chinese legend living in the southern sea.

long_description.id: Jiaoren adalah makhluk mirip manusia ikan dalam legenda Tiongkok yang hidup di laut selatan. Mereka juga disebut Quanxian atau Quanke.
long_description.en: Jiaoren are merperson like beings in Chinese legend living in the southern sea. They are also called Quanxian or Quanke.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita, air mata mereka menjadi mutiara. Jiaoren digambarkan mahir menenun kain yang tidak basah di air.

long_description.id: Bowuzhi karya Zhang Hua dan Soushen Ji sama-sama menempatkan jiaoren di Laut Selatan: mereka hidup di air seperti ikan, tetap menenun, dan matanya mengeluarkan mutiara saat menangis. Shuyi Ji menyamakan jiaoren dengan quanxian atau quanke, menyebut kain jiao yang dijual di pasar Yangzhou, dan menyebut sutra jiao dari Laut Selatan yang tidak basah di air.
long_description.en: The Bowuzhi of Zhang Hua and the Soushen Ji both place jiaoren in the South Sea: they live in water like fish, keep weaving, and their eyes shed pearls when they weep. The Shuyi Ji equates jiaoren with the quanxian or quanke, mentions jiao cloth sold at the market of Yangzhou, and describes jiao silk from the South Sea that does not get wet in water.

long_description.id: Dalam karya sastra, Koizumi Yakumo menulis Koujin no kansha, kisah jiaoren yang diusir dari istana naga, diselamatkan seorang lelaki, lalu membalas budi dengan permata dari air matanya.
long_description.en: In literature, Koizumi Yakumo wrote Koujin no kansha, the story of a jiaoren driven from the dragon palace, rescued by a man, who repays him with jewels formed from its tears.

short_description.id: Momo, singkatan dari "Missouri Monster", adalah kriptid besar berbulu gelap mirip manusia yang dilaporkan terlihat di pedesaan Missouri pada musim panas 1972.
short_description.en: Momo, short for "Missouri Monster", is a large, dark-haired humanoid cryptid reported in rural Missouri in the summer of 1972.

long_description.id: Momo digambarkan sebagai makhluk humanoid besar berbulu yang dikabarkan terlihat di pedesaan Missouri. Saksi menyebutnya menyerupai manusia atau kera berkaki dua setinggi sekitar 7 kaki (2,1 meter), tertutup rambut gelap, dan mengeluarkan bau busuk. Namanya merupakan singkatan dari Missouri Monster.
long_description.en: Momo is described as a large, hairy humanoid said to have been sighted in rural Missouri. Witnesses said it resembled a human or bipedal ape about 7 feet (2.1 m) tall, covered in dark hair and giving off a putrid odor. Its name is short for Missouri Monster.

long_description.id: Kegemparan Momo dimulai pada 11 Juli 1972 di pinggiran kota Louisiana, Missouri, ketika dua anak laki-laki sedang bermain di halaman. Kakak mereka, Doris, melihat sosok hitam berbulu setinggi enam atau tujuh kaki yang berdiri seperti manusia di dekat pohon. Makhluk itu berbercak darah, tampak mengepit anjing mati, wajahnya tertutup rambut, dan seolah tidak berleher.
long_description.en: The Momo scare began on July 11, 1972, on the outskirts of Louisiana, Missouri, when two young boys were playing in their yard. Their older sister Doris saw a black, hairy figure six or seven feet tall standing like a man by a tree. It was flecked with blood, apparently carrying a dead dog, its face hidden by hair, and it seemed to have no neck.

long_description.id: Laporan lain menyusul sepanjang Juli dan Agustus 1972. Seorang saksi bernama Harrison menggambarkan bau yang ia cium sebagai bau apak seperti kuda atau bau sampah yang kuat, dan seorang warga lain melihat makhluk itu berlari masuk ke hutan. Sebuah regu berisi 20 orang dibentuk untuk memburunya, tetapi tidak berhasil.
long_description.en: Further reports followed through July and August 1972. A witness named Harrison described the smell he encountered as a moldy horse or strong garbage smell, and another resident saw the creature dash into the woods. A 20-person posse was formed to hunt it, without success.

long_description.id: Berbeda dengan Fouke Monster atau Honey Island Swamp monster, Momo tidak menjadi daya tarik wisata yang besar. Meski begitu, taman hiburan Six Flags St. Louis pernah memiliki wahana bernama Momo (1973–1994), dan pada 2019 dirilis film dokudrama Momo: The Missouri Monster.
long_description.en: Unlike the Fouke Monster or the Honey Island Swamp monster, Momo did not become a major tourist attraction. Even so, Six Flags St. Louis had a ride named after it (1973–1994), and in 2019 the docudrama Momo: The Missouri Monster was released.

short_description.id: Monachicchio adalah peri usil bertopi merah dalam cerita rakyat Lucania, yang di Grassano dianggap roh anak yang mati sebelum dibaptis.
short_description.en: The Monachicchio is a red-capped mischievous sprite of Lucanian folklore, held in Grassano to be the spirit of a child who died before baptism.

long_description.id: Monachicchio adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Lucania yang gambarannya berbeda di tiap daerah Basilicata. Menurut tradisi Grassano, ia roh anak yang mati sebelum dibaptis, berwajah elok, berhati lembut, dan memakai topi kecil merah bernama u cuppulicchi; siapa yang merebut topi itu akan mendapat koin emas di dalamnya. Menurut tradisi Matera, ia peri usil yang mengikat surai kuda dan ekor keledai, tetapi tidak pernah menimbulkan kerugian serius, dan keisengannya hanya berhenti bila topinya direbut.
long_description.en: The Monachicchio is a figure of Lucanian folklore whose description varies across Basilicata. In the Grassano tradition he is the spirit of a child who died before baptism, handsome and gentle, wearing a little red cap called u cuppulicchi; whoever snatches it gets the gold coins inside. In the Matera tradition he is a mischievous sprite that ties horses' manes and donkeys' tails but never does serious harm, and his pranks stop only when his cap is taken.

long_description.id: Monachicchio banyak kesamaan dengan Scazzamurrieddhru dan Munaciello dari Napoli, dan asal mitosnya dicari pada agama Romawi, yang memberi Lares dan Penates tugas melindungi orang mati dan rumah.
long_description.en: The Monachicchio has much in common with the Scazzamurrieddhru and the Neapolitan Munaciello, and its origin is traced to Roman religion, which entrusted the Lares and Penates with protecting the dead and the home.

long_description.id: Di Basilicata roh rumah ini juga disebut munaceddi atau monachicci; daerah lain punya padanannya sendiri, seperti linchetti di Toscana dan munacielli di Campania. Buku Cristo si è fermato ad Eboli karya Carlo Levi menggambarkan mereka berlari cepat di dalam rumah dan hanya bisa ditangkap dengan menyambar topi merah di kepala mereka.
long_description.en: In Basilicata these house spirits are also called munaceddi or monachicci; other regions have their own counterparts, such as the linchetti in Toscana and the munacielli in Campania. Carlo Levi's Cristo si è fermato ad Eboli describes them darting through the house, catchable only by grabbing the red cap on their heads.

statement.id: Monachicchio punya identitas sendiri, dan gambarannya berbeda dari satu daerah Basilicata ke daerah lain.

claims.quote: Seconda la tradizione di Grassano, in provincia di Matera, il Monachicchio è lo spirito di un bambino morto prima di ricevere il battesimo. Di bell'aspetto e di carattere gentile, porta in testa un berrettino di color rosso, detto u cuppulicchi

statement.id: Menurut tradisi Grassano di provinsi Matera, Monachicchio adalah roh anak yang mati sebelum dibaptis, berwajah elok dan berhati lembut, yang memakai topi kecil merah bernama u cuppulicchi.
statement.en: In the tradition of Grassano, province of Matera, the Monachicchio is the spirit of a child who died before baptism, handsome and gentle, wearing a little red cap called u cuppulicchi.

claims.quote: sa che se i compagni di gioco gli togliessero u cuppulicchi, ne raccoglierebbero le monetine d'oro che questo contiene.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi daerah Matera, Monachicchio peri usil yang keisengannya tidak pernah menimbulkan masalah serius.
statement.en: In the Matera tradition the Monachicchio is a mischievous sprite whose pranks never cause serious harm.

statement.en: In Basilicata these house spirits are called munaceddi and monachicchi interchangeably.

claims.quote: Se leggete qualche pagina di Cristo si è fermato ad Eboli di Carlo Levi vi divertirete con una descrizione di questi spiriti vivaci e irrequieti, presenti in Basilicata, che corrono per la casa veloci e imprendibili, afferrabili solo con una mossa veloce e fulminea per il berretto rosso che hanno in testa.

statement.id: Buku Cristo si è fermato ad Eboli karya Carlo Levi melukiskan roh-roh lincah di Basilicata ini berlari cepat di dalam rumah dan sulit ditangkap, kecuali dengan gerakan kilat menyambar topi (berretto) merah di kepala mereka.
statement.en: Carlo Levi's Cristo si è fermato ad Eboli describes these lively spirits of Basilicata running swiftly and elusively through the house, catchable only by a lightning grab at the red cap (berretto) on their heads.

claims.quote: Regione che vai, nome che trovi. Salvanelli in Veneto, linchetti in Toscana, pamarindi in Friuli, farfareddi in Sicilia, monachicci in Basilicata, munacielli in Campania

statement.id: Setiap daerah punya nama sendiri untuk roh-roh kecil ini: salvanelli di Veneto, linchetti di Toscana, pamarindi di Friuli, farfareddi di Sicilia, monachicci di Basilicata, dan munacielli di Campania.
statement.en: Each region has its own name for these little spirits: salvanelli in Veneto, linchetti in Tuscany (Toscana), pamarindi in Friuli, farfareddi in Sicily (Sicilia), monachicci in Basilicata and munacielli in Campania.

Source specifies a handsome gentle child spirit with a red cap and harmless pranks, without a distinct active manifestation that can be made imposing under the ordinary-human prohibition. Decline instead of inventing frightening anatomy, giant scale, or unclaimed powers that would distort its benevolent character. Two image calls total; all attempts preserved.

short_description.id: Xuangui adalah kura-kura ajaib dalam legenda Tiongkok, dengan kepala burung dan ekor ular.
short_description.en: Xuangui is a fabulous turtle in Chinese legend with a bird's head and a snake's tail.

long_description.id: Xuangui adalah kura-kura ajaib dalam legenda Tiongkok, dengan kepala burung dan ekor ular. Warnanya digambarkan hitam.
long_description.en: Xuangui is a fabulous turtle in Chinese legend with a bird's head and a snake's tail. It is described as black in colour.

long_description.id: Suaranya menyerupai kayu yang dibelah. Artikel menghubungkan habitatnya dengan Gunung Niuyang dan pencatatannya dengan bagian selatan Shan Hai Jing. Teks klasik menempatkan Xuangui di air Guai yang mengalir ke air Xianyi. Teks klasik mengaitkan pemakaiannya dengan perlindungan pendengaran; ini adalah keyakinan dalam cerita.
long_description.en: Its sound resembles splitting wood. The article links its home to Mount Niuyang and its account to the southern section of the Shan Hai Jing. The classical text places Xuangui in the Guai water flowing into the Xianyi water. The classical text associates wearing it with protection of hearing, a belief within the narrative.

long_description.id: Gunung Niuyang, tempat air Guai bermula, digambarkan kaya logam merah di sisi selatan dan logam putih di sisi utara. Dalam Shanhaijing Guangzhu, Wu Renchen menyandingkan Xuangui dengan kura-kura E dari Laut Selatan yang disebut Bencao Shiyi, mengikuti penjelasan Li Shizhen. Edisi Siku Quanshu mencatat bahwa ekornya runcing dan suaranya seperti kayu dipecah.
long_description.en: Mount Niuyang, where the Guai water rises, is described as rich in red metal on its southern side and white metal on its northern side. In the Shanhaijing Guangzhu, Wu Renchen sets Xuangui beside the E turtle of the South Sea named in the Bencao Shiyi, following Li Shizhen. The Siku Quanshu edition notes that its tail is pointed and its sound like breaking wood.

statement.id: Artikel Wikipedia mengutip Shan Hai Jing (山海經): dari Gunung Niuyang (杻陽之山) keluar air Guai (怪水) yang banyak berisi Xuangui berkepala burung dan berekor ular, dengan suara seperti kayu yang dipecah.
statement.en: The Wikipedia article quotes the Shan Hai Jing (山海經): the Guai water (怪水) rises on Mount Niuyang (杻陽之山) and holds many Xuangui with bird heads and snake tails, whose sound is like breaking wood.

claims.quote: 佩之不聾可以為底〈郭曰底躪也為猶治也外傳曰疾不可為一作底猶病愈也　任臣案本草拾遺曰鶚龜生南海狀如龜二三尺兩目在側如鶚李時珍釋云山海經旋龜鳥首虺尾乃此𩔖也

statement.id: Dalam Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注), Wu Renchen (任臣) mengutip Bencao Shiyi (本草拾遺) tentang kura-kura E (鶚龜) dari Laut Selatan (南海) yang berwujud kura-kura dengan mata di sisi seperti burung elang ikan, dan penjelasan Li Shizhen (李時珍) bahwa Xuangui berkepala burung dan berekor ular dalam Shan Hai Jing termasuk jenis ini.
statement.en: In the Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注), Wu Renchen (任臣) cites the Bencao Shiyi (本草拾遺) on the E turtle (鶚龜) of the South Sea (南海), turtle-shaped with eyes at the sides like an osprey, and Li Shizhen (李時珍), who explains that the bird-headed, snake-tailed Xuangui of the Shan Hai Jing is of this kind.

claims.quote: 其中多𤣥龜其狀如龜而鳥首虺尾〈虺尾銳〉其名曰旋龜其音如判木〈如破木聲〉佩之不聾可以為底〈底躪也為猶治也外傳曰疾不可為一作底猶病愈也〉

statement.id: Edisi Siku Quanshu (四庫全書本) memuat catatan bahwa ekor Xuangui runcing (虺尾銳), suaranya seperti kayu dipecah (如破木聲), dan kata 底 dijelaskan sebagai 躪 atau "mengobati", dengan tafsiran lain bahwa 底 berarti sembuh dari penyakit.
statement.en: The Siku Quanshu edition (四庫全書本) carries notes that Xuangui's tail is pointed (虺尾銳), that its sound is like breaking wood (如破木聲), and that 底 is glossed as 躪 or "to treat", with an alternative reading of 底 as recovery from illness.

claims.quote: 又東三百七十里，曰杻〈音紐〉陽之山，其陽多赤金，其陰多白金〈銀也，見《爾雅》。山南爲陽，山北爲陰〉

statement.id: Teks klasik menempatkan Gunung Niuyang (杻陽之山) tiga ratus tujuh puluh li lebih ke timur, dengan banyak logam merah di sisi selatan dan logam putih di sisi utara.
statement.en: The classical text places Mount Niuyang (杻陽之山) three hundred and seventy li further east, with much red metal on its southern side and white metal on its northern side.

short_description.id: Lili adalah hewan legendaris mirip babi dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Lili is a piglike legendary animal in Chinese tradition.

long_description.id: Lili adalah hewan legendaris mirip babi dalam tradisi Tiongkok. Kakinya memiliki tonjolan seperti taji pada kaki ayam.
long_description.en: Lili is a piglike legendary animal in Chinese tradition. Its feet have projections compared to the rear spur of a chicken's foot.

long_description.id: Suaranya menyerupai gonggongan anjing. Kemunculannya dikaitkan dengan kegiatan pembangunan di suatu tempat. Bagian selatan kedua Shan Hai Jing menempatkan Lili pada Gunung Gui. Teks klasik menamai hewan bertaji dan bersuara anjing ini Lili.
long_description.en: Its voice resembles a dog's bark. Its appearance is associated with construction work in a locality. The second southern section of the Shan Hai Jing places Lili on Mount Gui. The classical text names this spurred animal with a doglike voice Lili.

long_description.id: Edisi Siku Quanshu dan Shanhaijing Guangzhu menulis namanya Lili (狸力). Edisi Siku Quanshu menyebut air Ying di Gunung Gui yang mengalir ke air Merah dengan giok putih dan butiran cinnabar. Guo Pu mencatat varian tulisan 狸刀, sedangkan Wu Renchen mengutip Pianya yang menyebut Lili anak babi bertaji. Wikipedia merujuk bagian yang sama untuk wujud mirip anak babi, taji, suara anjing, dan pertanda pekerjaan tanah.
long_description.en: The Siku Quanshu edition and the Shanhaijing Guangzhu write the name Lili (狸力). The Siku Quanshu edition mentions the Ying water on Mount Gui flowing into the Red water, with white jade and cinnabar grains. Guo Pu records the variant 狸刀, while Wu Renchen cites the Pianya, which calls Lili a spurred piglet. Wikipedia cites the same section for the piglet shape, the spurs, the dog-like voice and the omen of earthworks.

statement.id: Teks klasik menamai hewan bertaji dan bersuara anjing ini Lili.
statement.en: The classical text names this spurred animal with a doglike voice Lili.

claims.quote: 有獸焉其狀如䐁有距其音如狗吠其名曰狸力〈郭曰一作狸刀任臣案駢雅云狸力距䐁也〉見則其縣多土功

statement.id: Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注) menulis namanya 狸力 (Lili); catatan Guo Pu (郭) menyebut varian tulisan 狸刀, dan Wu Renchen (任臣) mengutip Pianya (駢雅) yang menyebut Lili sebagai anak babi bertaji.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注) writes the name 狸力 (Lili); Guo Pu's note (郭) records a variant written 狸刀, and Wu Renchen (任臣) cites the Pianya (駢雅), which calls Lili a spurred piglet.

claims.quote: 東望長右〈皆山名〉英水出焉西南流注于赤水其中多白玉〈尸子曰水方折者有玉員折者有珠〉

statement.id: Edisi Siku Quanshu (四庫全書本) menyebut air Ying (英水) di Gunung Gui mengalir ke barat daya menuju air Merah (赤水) dan banyak mengandung giok putih.
statement.en: The Siku Quanshu edition (四庫全書本) says the Ying water (英水) on Mount Gui flows southwest into the Red water (赤水) and holds much white jade.

statement.id: Edisi yang sama menyebut butiran cinnabar di sana, lalu seekor binatang mirip anak babi bertaji, bersuara seperti anjing menyalak, bernama Lili (狸力); bila ia terlihat, daerahnya akan banyak pekerjaan tanah.
statement.en: The same edition mentions cinnabar grains there, then a piglet-like animal with spurs and a voice like a barking dog named Lili (狸力); when it is seen, its county will have much earthwork.

statement.en: The Wikipedia article cites the Nanci Er Jing (南次二經) section of the Shan Hai Jing for the piglet shape, the spurs, the dog-like voice and the omen of earthworks.

short_description.id: Luoluo adalah burung pemakan manusia yang tercatat dalam Shan Hai Jing.
short_description.en: Luoluo is a human eating bird recorded in the Shan Hai Jing.

long_description.id: Luoluo adalah burung pemakan manusia yang tercatat dalam Shan Hai Jing. Kisah burung Luoluo menempatkannya pada Gunung Lai.
long_description.en: Luoluo is a human eating bird recorded in the Shan Hai Jing. The account of the Luoluo bird places it on Mount Lai.

long_description.id: Nama Luoluo juga dipakai untuk hewan buas kebiruan mirip harimau dalam bagian lain teks. Guo Pu menyatakan bahwa ciri burung Luoluo tidak dijelaskan secara rinci. Teks klasik menyebut pepohonan cendana dan murbei di Gunung Lai, tempat banyak Luoluo. Dalam bagian Haiwai Bei Jing, 羅羅 disebut sebagai binatang hijau kebiruan (青) yang berbentuk seperti harimau.
long_description.en: The name Luoluo is also used for a bluish tigerlike beast elsewhere in the text. Guo Pu notes that the Luoluo bird's characteristics are not explained in detail. The classical text mentions sandalwood and mulberry trees on Mount Lai, where Luoluo are numerous. The Overseas North section describes 羅羅 as a blue-green (青) beast shaped like a tiger.

long_description.id: Tentang binatang luoluo yang mirip harimau, Wu Renchen mengutip Pianya yang menyebut harimau biru dengan nama itu, dan Tianzhong Ji yang mencatat bahwa di Yunnan harimau juga disebut luoluo.
long_description.en: On the tiger-like luoluo beast, Wu Renchen cites the Pianya, which gives that name to a blue tiger, and the Tianzhong Ji, which records that in Yunnan the tiger is also called luoluo.

short_description.id: Mich adalah dewa laut berwujud ikan yang dipuja penduduk asli Kamchatka, dewa yang hanya memikirkan dirinya sendiri.
short_description.en: Mich is a fish-shaped sea god worshipped by the indigenous people of Kamchatka, a god who thinks only of himself.

long_description.id: Penduduk asli Kamchatka memuja laut dengan nama Mich dan menggambarkan dewa itu berwujud ikan; mereka menganggapnya salah satu dewa pertama. Mich hanya memikirkan dirinya sendiri: bila ia mengirim ikan ke pantai, itu hanya agar orang mencarikan kayu untuk kanonya, bukan untuk menolong manusia.
long_description.en: The indigenous people of Kamchatka worship the sea as Mich and depict the god as a fish, counting him among the first deities. Mich thinks only of himself: if he sends fish to the shore, it is only so people will fetch wood for his canoes, not to help them.

long_description.id: Sebuah kamus mitologi lama memuat keterangan yang sama tentang dewa laut orang Kamchadal, yang namanya rusak dalam teks pindaian ('Mi¿g'). Dewa itu digambarkan berwujud ikan dan hanya memikirkan dirinya sendiri: ikan yang dikirimnya ke pantai sebenarnya mencari kayu, bukan untuk menjadi makanan manusia.
long_description.en: An old mythology dictionary gives the same account of the Kamchadals' sea god, whose name is garbled in the scanned text ('Mi¿g'). The god is pictured as a fish who thinks only of himself: the fish he sends to the shore are really looking for wood, not meant as food for people.

long_description.id: Menurut kamus itu, orang Kamchadal tidak memberi apa pun kepada dewanya karena tidak mengharapkan manfaat apa pun darinya; bangsa ini tidak percaya bahwa dewa dapat berbuat baik kepada manusia.
long_description.en: According to the dictionary, the Kamchadals give their god nothing because they expect no benefit from him; these peoples do not believe a deity can do good to people.

short_description.id: Sharlie adalah ular laut dalam cerita rakyat Idaho, mirip Loch Ness Monster, yang dipercaya hidup di Payette Lake dekat McCall [sharlie-c01].
short_description.en: Sharlie is a sea serpent of Idaho folklore, much like the Loch Ness Monster, believed to live in Payette Lake near McCall [sharlie-c01].

long_description.id: Sharlie adalah ular laut dalam cerita rakyat Idaho yang dipercaya sebagian orang hidup di Payette Lake dekat McCall [sharlie-c01]. Rujukan pertamanya mungkin kepercayaan penduduk asli Amerika bahwa roh jahat tinggal di danau itu [sharlie-c02].
long_description.en: Sharlie is a sea serpent of Idaho folklore believed by some to live in Payette Lake near McCall [sharlie-c01]. Its first reference may be the Native American belief that an evil spirit dwelled in the lake [sharlie-c02].

long_description.id: Penampakan pertama oleh pendatang Barat tercatat pada tahun 1920 [sharlie-c03]. Pada tahun 1944, saksi menggambarkannya sepanjang 30 hingga 35 kaki dengan kepala mirip dinosaurus dan punuk seperti unta [sharlie-c04]. Nama Sharlie berasal dari sayembara The Star News pada tahun 1954 [sharlie-c05], dan penampakan terakhir yang tercatat terjadi pada tahun 1997 [sharlie-c06].
long_description.en: The first sighting by western settlers was documented in 1920 [sharlie-c03]. In 1944, witnesses described it as 30 to 35 feet long with a dinosaur-like head and camel-like humps [sharlie-c04]. The name Sharlie came from a contest held by The Star News in 1954 [sharlie-c05], and the last documented sighting was in 1997 [sharlie-c06].

long_description.id: Pada September 1946, ular itu dilaporkan terlihat oleh dua puluh orang sekaligus. Nama Sharlie diajukan oleh Lelsle Hennefer Tury dari Springfield, Virginia, sebagai rujukan pada ungkapan populer Jack Pearl di acara radionya. Kliping dan dokumen tentang Sharlie kini tersimpan dalam berkas setebal 66 halaman di koleksi perpustakaan umum McCall.
long_description.en: In September 1946 the serpent was reportedly seen by a group of twenty people at once. The name Sharlie was submitted by Lelsle Hennefer Tury of Springfield, Virginia, as a reference to a popular catch phrase of Jack Pearl's radio show. Clippings and documents about Sharlie are now kept in a 66-page file in the McCall public library collection.

claims.quote: In Idaho folklore, Sharlie (Slimy Slim, The Twilight Dragon of Payette Lake) is the name given to a sea serpent much like the Loch Ness Monster that is believed by some to live in the deep alpine waters of Payette Lake near McCall, Idaho.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Idaho, Sharlie (juga Slimy Slim atau The Twilight Dragon of Payette Lake) adalah ular laut mirip Loch Ness Monster yang dipercaya sebagian orang hidup di perairan dalam Payette Lake dekat McCall, Idaho.
statement.en: In Idaho folklore, Sharlie (also Slimy Slim or The Twilight Dragon of Payette Lake) is a sea serpent much like the Loch Ness Monster, believed by some to live in the deep waters of Payette Lake near McCall, Idaho.

claims.quote: The first reference to the sea serpent may be the belief of Native Americans, predating western settlement of the area, that an evil spirit dwelled in the lake.

statement.id: Rujukan pertama tentang ular laut ini mungkin kepercayaan penduduk asli Amerika, sebelum permukiman orang Barat, bahwa roh jahat tinggal di danau itu.
statement.en: The first reference may be the Native American belief, predating western settlement, that an evil spirit dwelled in the lake.

claims.quote: The first documented sighting by western settlers occurred in 1920 when workers cutting ties at the upper end of the lake thought they saw a log in the lake.

statement.id: Penampakan pertama yang tercatat oleh pendatang Barat terjadi pada tahun 1920, ketika pekerja di ujung atas danau mengira melihat sebatang kayu.
statement.en: The first documented sighting by western settlers was in 1920, when workers at the upper end of the lake thought they saw a log.

claims.quote: In August 1944, the serpent was reportedly seen by several groups of people who described it as 30 to 35 feet in length with a dinosaur-like head, pronounced jaws, humps like a camel, and shell-like skin.

statement.id: Pada Agustus 1944, beberapa kelompok orang melaporkan melihatnya sepanjang 30 hingga 35 kaki, berkepala mirip dinosaurus, berpunuk seperti unta, dan berkulit seperti cangkang.
statement.en: In August 1944, several groups reported it as 30 to 35 feet long with a dinosaur-like head, camel-like humps and shell-like skin.

claims.quote: In 1954 A. Boone McCallum, Editor of The Star News held a contest to name the serpent of Payette Lake.

statement.id: Pada tahun 1954, A. Boone McCallum, editor The Star News, mengadakan sayembara untuk menamai ular Payette Lake.
statement.en: In 1954, A. Boone McCallum, editor of The Star News, held a contest to name the Payette Lake serpent.

claims.quote: Sharlie was reportedly sighted dozens of times between 1956 and the last documented sighting in 1997.

statement.id: Sharlie dilaporkan terlihat puluhan kali antara tahun 1956 dan penampakan terakhir yang tercatat pada tahun 1997.
statement.en: Sharlie was reportedly sighted dozens of times between 1956 and the last documented sighting in 1997.

claims.quote: 66 pages of subject files containing and related to Sharlie

statement.id: Koleksi Perpustakaan Umum McCall menyimpan 66 halaman berkas subjek tentang Sharlie.
statement.en: The McCall Public Library collection holds 66 pages of subject files about Sharlie.

claims.quote: In September 1946 the serpent was reportedly sighted by a group of twenty people.

statement.id: Pada September 1946, ular itu dilaporkan terlihat oleh sekelompok dua puluh orang.
statement.en: In September 1946 the serpent was reportedly sighted by a group of twenty people.

claims.quote: The winning name, “Sharlie”, was submitted by Lelsle Hennefer Tury of Springfield, Virginia.

statement.id: Nama pemenang, "Sharlie", diajukan oleh Lelsle Hennefer Tury dari Springfield, Virginia.
statement.en: The winning name, "Sharlie", was submitted by Lelsle Hennefer Tury of Springfield, Virginia.

claims.quote: This was a reference to the popular catch phrase often spoken by Jack Pearl during his old time radio show.

statement.id: Nama itu merujuk pada ungkapan populer yang sering diucapkan Jack Pearl dalam acara radionya.
statement.en: The name referred to a popular catch phrase often spoken by Jack Pearl on his old-time radio show.

short_description.id: Sisimito adalah kriptid mirip gorila berkepala seperti manusia dalam cerita rakyat Belize dan Honduras, dikenal pula di Guatemala dan Nicaragua [sisimito-c01, sisimito-c02].
short_description.en: The Sisimito is a gorilla-like cryptid with a human-like head in Belizean and Honduran folklore, also known in Guatemala and Nicaragua [sisimito-c01, sisimito-c02].

long_description.id: Sisimito adalah kriptid mirip gorila yang berjalan tegak dalam cerita rakyat Belize dan Honduras [sisimito-c01], juga dikenal di Guatemala dan Nicaragua [sisimito-c02]. Ia berjari empat tanpa ibu jari dan berkaki terbalik [sisimito-c03]. Namanya diyakini berasal dari kata Nahuatl Tzitzimitl [sisimito-c05], dan orang Garifuna menyebutnya Sismidu [sisimito-c04].
long_description.en: The Sisimito is an upright, gorilla-like cryptid of Belizean and Honduran folklore [sisimito-c01], also known in Guatemala and Nicaragua [sisimito-c02]. It has four fingers without thumbs and backward-facing feet [sisimito-c03]. Its name is believed to come from the Nahuatl word Tzitzimitl [sisimito-c05], and the Garifuna call it Sismidu [sisimito-c04].

long_description.id: Menurut legenda Honduras, ia menculik perempuan [sisimito-c06] tetapi memakan buah beri dan bukan pemburu [sisimito-c07]. Dalam legenda Belize, ia memangsa manusia [sisimito-c08], tinggal di gua dan tanah berbatu [sisimito-c09], menyamar sebagai manusia untuk memancing korbannya [sisimito-c11], dan menyerang orang yang merusak hutan [sisimito-c13]. Ia takut air dan anjing [sisimito-c10], dan cara terampuh mengusirnya adalah membakar rambutnya [sisimito-c15].
long_description.en: In Honduran legend it kidnaps women [sisimito-c06] but eats berries and is not a hunter [sisimito-c07]. In Belizean legend it feasts on humans [sisimito-c08], lives in caves and on rocky land [sisimito-c09], takes human form to lure victims [sisimito-c11], and attacks those who destroy the forest [sisimito-c13]. It fears water and dogs [sisimito-c10], and the surest way to be rid of it is to set its hair on fire [sisimito-c15].

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Honduras yang dikumpulkan Javier Durón Padilla, sisimite digambarkan sebagai hewan mirip monyet berwajah seperti manusia yang tinggal di pegunungan dan mudah jatuh cinta. Ia konon suka memakan abu panas dan mencium batang pohon yang baru terbakar, meski vegetarian, sehingga sering terlihat setelah pembakaran lahan. Karena kakinya terbalik, jejaknya selalu tampak menuju arah yang berlawanan. Dalam semua kisahnya ia memperoleh seorang anak, yang kelak membunuhnya.
long_description.en: In Honduran folklore collected by Javier Durón Padilla, the sisimite is a monkey-like animal with a human-like face that lives in the mountains and falls in love easily. It is said to like eating hot ash and smelling freshly burned tree trunks, though vegetarian, so it is often seen after land is burned. Because its feet are reversed, its tracks always seem to point the opposite way. In all its tales it fathers a child, who later kills it.

claims.quote: In Belizean and Honduran folklore, the Sisimito (alternatively called Sisimite, Sisimita, Súkara, and Itacayo) is a bipedal upright gorilla-like cryptid that possesses a head much like a human, with long hair or fur covering its body.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Belize dan Honduras, Sisimito (juga Sisimite, Sisimita, Súkara, dan Itacayo) adalah kriptid mirip gorila yang berjalan tegak, berkepala mirip manusia, dan bertubuh berbulu panjang.
statement.en: In Belizean and Honduran folklore, the Sisimito (also Sisimite, Sisimita, Súkara and Itacayo) is an upright, gorilla-like cryptid with a human-like head and long hair covering its body.

claims.quote: It is also referred to as "the Mexican Bigfoot", though it is also known in the neighboring countries of Guatemala and Nicaragua.

statement.id: Ia juga disebut "Bigfoot Meksiko" dan dikenal pula di Guatemala dan Nicaragua.
statement.en: It is also called "the Mexican Bigfoot" and is known in Guatemala and Nicaragua as well.

claims.quote: It is said to have four fingers on each hand and no thumbs, ape-like facial features, and backward-facing feet with no knees.

statement.id: Ia konon berjari empat tanpa ibu jari, berwajah seperti kera, dan berkaki terbalik tanpa lutut.
statement.en: It is said to have four fingers and no thumbs, ape-like features, and backward-facing feet with no knees.

claims.quote: Its name differs between ethnic groups, for example, the Garifuna call it Sismidu.

statement.id: Namanya berbeda antarsuku; misalnya orang Garifuna menyebutnya Sismidu.
statement.en: Its name differs between ethnic groups; the Garifuna call it Sismidu.

claims.quote: The name has no true English translation and it is believed to have come from the Nahuatl word, Tzitzimitl.

statement.id: Namanya diyakini berasal dari kata Nahuatl Tzitzimitl.
statement.en: The name is believed to come from the Nahuatl word Tzitzimitl.

claims.quote: According to Honduran legends, it is believed that the Sisimite targets and kidnaps human women.

statement.id: Menurut legenda Honduras, Sisimite mengincar dan menculik perempuan manusia.
statement.en: According to Honduran legends, the Sisimite targets and kidnaps human women.

claims.quote: Aguilar also explains that the Sisimite feeds on the wild berries from the mountains and that it is not a carnivorous being or a hunter

statement.id: Menurut Aguilar, Sisimite memakan buah beri liar dari pegunungan dan bukan pemakan daging atau pemburu.
statement.en: According to Aguilar, the Sisimite eats wild berries from the mountains and is not a carnivore or hunter.

claims.quote: In Belizean legend, the Sisimite is said to also feast on humans.

statement.id: Dalam legenda Belize, Sisimite juga memangsa manusia.
statement.en: In Belizean legend, the Sisimite also feasts on humans.

claims.quote: The Sismite is said to live in high forest areas and lives in caves and on rocky land.

statement.id: Sismite konon tinggal di hutan dataran tinggi, di gua, dan di tanah berbatu.
statement.en: It is said to live in high forest areas, in caves and on rocky land.

claims.quote: Though fierce and malevolent towards humans, he is afraid of water and dogs and will avoid them at all costs.

statement.id: Meski ganas dan jahat terhadap manusia, ia takut air dan anjing.
statement.en: Though fierce and malevolent towards humans, he is afraid of water and dogs.

claims.quote: The Sisimite is believed to often assume human form in order to lure people out of villages with the purpose of killing them.

statement.id: Sisimite dipercaya sering menyamar sebagai manusia untuk memancing orang keluar desa lalu membunuhnya.
statement.en: The Sisimite is believed to take human form to lure people out of villages and kill them.

claims.quote: Because of this, he is sometimes confused with Xtabay or La Llorona.

statement.id: Karena itu ia kadang disamakan dengan Xtabay atau La Llorona.
statement.en: Because of this, he is sometimes confused with Xtabay or La Llorona.

claims.quote: the Sisimite is also believed to attack men who are killing animals needlessly or destroying the forest.

statement.id: Sisimite juga dipercaya menyerang pria yang membunuh hewan tanpa perlu atau merusak hutan.
statement.en: The Sisimite is also believed to attack men who kill animals needlessly or destroy the forest.

claims.quote: If one dances in a circle, the Sisimite will try to follow them. However, due to his backward-facing feet he would trip and fall.

statement.id: Jika seseorang menari melingkar, Sisimite akan mengikutinya, tetapi kakinya yang terbalik membuatnya tersandung dan jatuh.
statement.en: If one dances in a circle, the Sisimite follows but trips and falls because of its backward-facing feet.

claims.quote: The ultimate way to get rid of the Sisimite is to set fire to his long hair.

statement.id: Cara terampuh mengusir Sisimite adalah membakar rambutnya yang panjang.
statement.en: The ultimate way to get rid of the Sisimite is to set fire to his long hair.

claims.quote: The Sisimite is featured in the 1951 B-movie Bride of the Gorilla, directed by Curt Siodmak.

statement.id: Sisimite muncul dalam film kelas B tahun 1951, Bride of the Gorilla, karya Curt Siodmak.
statement.en: The Sisimite appears in the 1951 B-movie Bride of the Gorilla, directed by Curt Siodmak.

claims.quote: Según se cuenta, el sisimite es un animal parecido a un mono, su cara es como la de una persona, vive en las montañas y es muy enamorado

statement.en: According to the tale, the sisimite is a monkey-like animal with a face like a person's, living in the mountains and very amorous.

claims.quote: En todos los relatos que se cuentan se dice que procrea un hijo, que es el que más tarde le da muerte.

statement.id: Dalam semua kisah yang diceritakan, ia memperoleh seorang anak, dan anak itulah yang kelak membunuhnya.

claims.quote: Al sisimite se le ha visto después de una quema, ya que al parecer le agrada comer ceniza caliente y oler los troncos de los árboles recién quemados, aunque es vegetariano.

statement.id: Sisimite pernah terlihat setelah pembakaran lahan karena tampaknya ia suka memakan abu panas (ceniza caliente) dan mencium batang pohon yang baru terbakar, meskipun ia vegetarian.
statement.en: The sisimite has been seen after a burn, as it apparently likes to eat hot ash and smell freshly burned tree trunks, although it is vegetarian.

claims.quote: Si camina para adelante deja las huellas como si fuera caminando para atrás, y si camina para atrás, deja su rastro como si fuera para adelante.

statement.id: Bila ia berjalan maju, jejaknya tampak seperti berjalan mundur, dan bila berjalan mundur, jejaknya tampak seperti berjalan maju.
statement.en: When it walks forward its tracks look as if it were walking backward, and when it walks backward its trail looks as if it were walking forward.

claims.quote: Cuentan que nunca la encontraron, pero hallaron por todo el monte pares de huellas al revés que llegaban juntas a la cima de un cerro.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, gadis yang hilang tidak pernah ditemukan, tetapi di seluruh hutan ditemukan pasangan jejak kaki terbalik yang bersama-sama menuju puncak bukit.

claims.quote: Por eso dijeron que había sido el sisimite come ceniza que se había llevado a la muchacha para siempre.

statement.id: Karena itu orang berkata bahwa sisimite pemakan abu (come ceniza) telah membawa gadis itu untuk selamanya.
statement.en: So people said it had been the ash-eating sisimite that had carried the girl off forever.

short_description.id: Boyi adalah makhluk mirip domba dengan sembilan ekor dan empat telinga dalam Shan Hai Jing.
short_description.en: Boyi is a sheeplike creature with nine tails and four ears in the Shan Hai Jing.

long_description.id: Boyi adalah makhluk mirip domba dengan sembilan ekor dan empat telinga dalam Shan Hai Jing. Matanya terletak pada punggung.
long_description.en: Boyi is a sheeplike creature with nine tails and four ears in the Shan Hai Jing. Its eyes are located on its back.

long_description.id: Tradisi yang dikutip menganggap mengenakan kulitnya dapat menyingkirkan rasa takut. Teks klasik menempatkan Boyi pada Gunung Ji. Gunung tempat Boyi dicatat memiliki giok di sisi selatan dan pepohonan ganjil di sisi utara. Dalam teks klasik, fungsi pelindung Boyi dinyatakan sebagai tidak merasa takut ketika memakainya.
long_description.en: The cited tradition treats wearing its hide as a way to dispel fear. The classical text places Boyi on Mount Ji. The mountain where Boyi is recorded has jade on its southern side and unusual trees on its northern side. The classical text describes Boyi as protecting its wearer from fear.

long_description.id: Gunung Ji termasuk rangkaian Que, bagian pertama Nanshan Jing. Tuzan karya Guo Pu menyebut Boyi mirip domba dengan mata di punggung, dan kulitnya boleh dikenakan oleh orang yang ingin tidak takut. Wu Renchen mencatat versi lain dalam Huiya, yaitu binatang mirip domba tanpa ekor, serta versi Wuhou Qing yang menyebut Gunung Mu, tetapi ia menilai keduanya keliru.
long_description.en: Mount Ji belongs to the Que range, the first part of the Nanshan Jing. Guo Pu's Tuzan says Boyi resembles a sheep with eyes on its back, and that its hide may be worn by anyone who wishes not to be afraid. Wu Renchen notes another version in the Huiya, a tailless sheep-like beast, and the Wuhou Qing's mention of Mount Mu, but judges both to be errors.

short_description.id: Knochenfund von Seweckenberge adalah "unicorn fosil" yang direkonstruksi pada akhir abad ke-17 dan awal abad ke-18 dari tulang-tulang zaman Pleistosen yang ditemukan pada 1663 di dekat Quedlinburg, Jerman.
short_description.en: The Seweckenberge bone find is a 'fossil unicorn' reconstructed in the late 17th and early 18th centuries from Pleistocene bones found in 1663 near Quedlinburg, Germany.

long_description.id: Temuan tulang Seweckenberge merujuk pada dugaan rekonstruksi seekor unicorn fosil pada akhir abad ke-17 atau awal abad ke-18. Pada 1663 para pekerja tambang gipsum dan batu kapur di perbukitan Seweckenberge, tenggara Quedlinburg di Sachsen-Anhalt, menemukan tulang-tulang mamalia besar dari zaman Pleistosen yang belum memfosil, termasuk tengkorak bertanduk, rusuk, tulang belakang, tulang belikat, dan tulang kaki.
long_description.en: The Seweckenberge bone find refers to the supposed reconstruction of a fossil unicorn in the late 17th or early 18th century. In 1663 workers quarrying gypsum and limestone in the Seweckenberge hills south-east of Quedlinburg in Saxony-Anhalt uncovered unfossilised Pleistocene bones of large mammals, including a skull with a horn, ribs, spine, shoulder blades and leg bones.

long_description.id: Otto von Guericke kemudian menulis bahwa di gunung Seveckenberg ditemukan kerangka unicorn dengan kepala terangkat dan tanduk panjang setebal paha manusia di dahinya; kerangka itu dipecahkan karena ketidaktahuan, lalu kepala, tanduk, dan sebagian tulangnya diserahkan kepada kepala biara perempuan Quedlinburg. Gambar "unicorn fosil" dengan hanya dua kaki depan kemudian diterbitkan oleh Michael Bernhard Valentini (1704) dan dalam Protogaea karya Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1749).
long_description.en: Otto von Guericke later wrote that a unicorn skeleton had been found in the Seveckenberg hill, with a raised head and a long horn as thick as a human thigh on its forehead; it was broken up through ignorance, and the head, horn and some bones were given to the princess-abbess of Quedlinburg. Pictures of a 'fossil unicorn' with only two forelegs were later published by Michael Bernhard Valentini (1704) and in Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz's Protogaea (1749).

long_description.id: Berdasarkan gambar-gambar itu, tulangnya dapat dikenali sebagai milik beberapa hewan berbeda: badak berbulu atau hewan berkuku lain, mamut berbulu, dan narwal masa kini sebagai "tanduk"-nya. Rekonstruksi ini menjadi ikon kriptozoologi dan paleontologi awal; banyak penulis kemudian keliru menyebut Guericke sebagai penemu dan perakitnya, padahal sebenarnya ia tidak terlibat.
long_description.en: From those pictures the bones can be assigned to several different animals: a woolly rhinoceros or other hoofed animal, the woolly mammoth, and a modern narwhal as the 'horn'. The reconstruction became an icon of cryptozoology and early palaeontology; many later writers wrongly named Guericke as its finder and assembler, though he in fact took no part.

statement.en: The Seweckenberge bone find refers to the supposed reconstruction of a fossil unicorn in the late 17th or early 18th century; it is sometimes called the Guericke-Einhorn, though Guericke had no part in the find or the reconstruction.

statement.id: Di perbukitan Seweckenberge, tenggara Quedlinburg di Sachsen-Anhalt (Jerman), batu kapur dan gipsum ditambang sejak Abad Pertengahan; pada 1663 para pekerja menemukan di sebuah rongga tulang mamalia besar dari Pleistosen (Pleistozän) yang belum memfosil.
statement.en: In the Seweckenberge hills south-east of Quedlinburg in Saxony-Anhalt (Germany), limestone and gypsum were quarried from the Middle Ages; in 1663 workers found unfossilised Pleistocene (Pleistozän) bones of large mammals in a cavity.

statement.en: The bones included a skull with the horn, ribs, spine, shoulder blades and leg bones; from the published 'reconstructions' they can be assigned to woolly rhinoceros or other ungulates, the woolly mammoth, and a modern narwhal as donor of the 'horn'.

statement.en: Guericke wrote that in 1663 near Quedlinburg, in a hill called Seveckenberg where gypsum is dug, the skeleton of a unicorn (Einhorns) was found in a rock fissure.

claims.quote: 1749, und damit mehr als 40 Jahre nach seinem Tod, wurde Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz’ Protogaea erstmals veröffentlicht. Darin übernahm er die Schilderung Guerickes fast wörtlich. Er fügte auch eine Tafel mit einem Kupferstich von Nikolaus Seeländer bei. Die Darstellung zeigt eine frappierende Ähnlichkeit mit Valentinis Abbildung aus dem Jahr 1704.

statement.id: Protogaea karya Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz terbit pertama 1749, lebih dari 40 tahun setelah ia wafat; ia mengutip uraian Guericke hampir kata demi kata dan menambahkan ukiran tembaga Nikolaus Seeländer yang sangat mirip gambar Michael Bernhard Valentini (Valentinis) tahun 1704 dalam Museum Museorum.
statement.en: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz's Protogaea was first published in 1749, over 40 years after his death; he took over Guericke's account almost verbatim and added a copperplate by Nikolaus Seeländer strikingly like Michael Bernhard Valentini's 1704 image in Museum Museorum.

statement.id: Unicorn Magdeburg (Magdeburger Einhorn, juga Guericke-Einhorn) adalah dugaan temuan fosil yang tercatat antara abad ke-17 dan ke-18, tersusun dari tengkorak badak berbulu, kaki mamut berbulu, dan tanduk narwal.
statement.en: The Magdeburg unicorn (Magdeburger Einhorn, also Guericke-Einhorn) is a supposed fossil find attested in the 17th–18th centuries, made up of a woolly rhinoceros skull, woolly mammoth legs and a narwhal horn.

short_description.id: Konpira Gongen adalah dewa Jepang dalam tradisi Shugendō yang berasal dari Gunung Kotohira, dikenal sebagai dewa pelaut niaga dan kami pelindung pelayaran.
short_description.en: Konpira Gongen is a Japanese god of the Shugendō tradition originating on Mount Kotohira, known as the god of merchant sailors and a guardian kami of seafarers.

long_description.id: Konpira Gongen (金毘羅権現) adalah dewa Jepang dalam aliran Shugendō yang berasal dari Gunung Kotohira di Kagawa. Ia adalah dewa pelaut niaga. Menurut legenda, ia muncul ketika seorang pendeta di Kuil Matsuo memanggil dewa Sungai Gangga, Kumbhīra, yang digambarkan sebagai dewa buaya Sungai Gangga dan diidentifikasi dengan yang pertama dari dua belas utusan roh yang berasal dari Bhaisajyaguru.
long_description.en: Konpira Gongen (金毘羅権現) is a Shugendō deity of Japan whose origins lie on Mount Kotohira in Kagawa Prefecture, and he is the god of merchant sailors. According to legend, he came into existence when a priest at Matsuo Temple summoned the Ganges deity Kumbhīra, described as a Ganges crocodile god and tied to the first of the twelve spirit messengers that proceed from Bhaisajyaguru.

long_description.id: Encyclopedia of Shinto menyebut Konpira sebagai kami pelindung pelaut dan nelayan, yang juga diyakini sebagai kami petir, kami air, kami pertanian, dan kami penjaga yang menjaga selagi kami lain pergi. Dewa Konpira adalah kami Jepang, tetapi ada pengaruh Buddha di Gunung Zōzu, dan di kawasan itu juga ada kegiatan Shugendō. Pada zaman Edo, Kumbhīra dari India dipadukan dengan Konpira, dan pemujaan menyebar bersama pelayaran dan jaringan transportasi. Di pedesaan, Konpira dipuja sebagai kami ular.
long_description.en: The Encyclopedia of Shinto presents Konpira as a guardian kami of seafarers and fishermen who is also believed to be a thunder kami, a water kami, an agricultural kami, and a guardian who keeps watch while other kami are away. The deity is a Japanese kami, but there is Buddhist influence at Mount Zōzu, where Shugendō was also practiced. In the Edo period the Indian Kumbhīra was conflated with Konpira and the cult spread along with shipping and transportation networks. In the countryside Konpira was worshipped as a serpent kami.

long_description.id: Seiring waktu, orang Jepang mulai memandang Konpira sebagai pelindung agama Buddha mereka. Kepercayaan kuat pada Konpira sebagai pelindung pelayaran yang aman terlihat dari banyaknya ema berbentuk kapal yang dipersembahkan kepada kuil.
long_description.en: Over time the Japanese came to regard Konpira as a protector of their Buddhist faith. Fervent belief in Konpira as a protector of safe sea travel is shown by the many boat ema offered at the shrine.

literal_meaning.id: Nama kuil diperkirakan berasal dari kotohiki, praktik magis melawan bunyi petir dengan bunyi koto.

claims.quote: As well as being a guardian kami of seafarers and fishermen, Konpira is believed to be a "thunder kami" (raijin), a water kami (suijin), an agricultural kami (nōkōjin), and a guardian kami who keeps watch while other kami are away (rusugami).

statement.id: Encyclopedia of Shinto menyebut bahwa selain sebagai kami pelindung para pelaut dan nelayan, Konpira diyakini sebagai kami petir (raijin), kami air (suijin), kami pertanian (nōkōjin), dan kami penjaga yang menjaga selagi kami lain pergi (rusugami).
statement.en: The Encyclopedia of Shinto says that, as well as being a guardian kami of seafarers and fishermen, Konpira is believed to be a thunder kami (raijin), a water kami (suijin), an agricultural kami (nōkōjin), and a guardian kami who keeps watch while other kami are away (rusugami).

statement.en: During the Edo period the Indian deity Kumbhīra, described as a dragon-king sea deity who protected the palace, was conflated with Konpira, and the cult spread along with the development of shipping and transportation networks.

short_description.id: Lagahoo adalah monster pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Trinidad and Tobago yang berkeliaran pada malam hari tanpa kepala dengan peti mati di lehernya [lagahoo-c01, lagahoo-c02].
short_description.en: The Lagahoo is a shapeshifting monster of Trinidad and Tobago folklore that roams at night headless, with a coffin on its neck [lagahoo-c01, lagahoo-c02].

long_description.id: Lagahoo adalah monster pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Trinidad and Tobago [lagahoo-c01]. Kata lagahoo berasal dari bahasa Prancis loup-garou, "manusia serigala" [lagahoo-c07]. Pada siang hari ia tampak seperti manusia, tetapi pada malam hari menjadi lelaki tanpa kepala dengan peti mati kayu di lehernya [lagahoo-c02], dihiasi tiga lilin menyala dan rantai besi yang terseret [lagahoo-c03].
long_description.en: The Lagahoo is a shapeshifting monster of Trinidad and Tobago folklore [lagahoo-c01]. The word lagahoo comes from the French loup-garou, "werewolf" [lagahoo-c07]. Human by day, at night it becomes a headless man with a wooden coffin on its neck [lagahoo-c02], topped by three lit candles, dragging an iron chain [lagahoo-c03].

long_description.id: Ia dapat berubah menjadi kuda, babi, kambing, atau makhluk mirip centaur [lagahoo-c04], dan dalam kutipan folklor Gerard Besson ia dapat mengubah wujudnya menjadi binatang atau bentuk apa pun serta berkeliaran di jalan atau hutan [lagahoo-c08]. Ia juga dapat mengubah ukurannya dari sangat kecil menjadi raksasa dalam sekejap [lagahoo-c05]; konon kadang ia setinggi itu hingga kepalanya hilang di atas pepohonan [lagahoo-c11].
long_description.en: It can become a horse, pig, goat or centaur-like creature [lagahoo-c04], and in the folklore passage quoted from Gerard Besson it could take the shape of any animal or form and wander streets or woods [lagahoo-c08]. It can also change its size from tiny to gigantic in an instant [lagahoo-c05]; people said that sometimes it grew so tall that its head disappeared above the trees [lagahoo-c11].

long_description.id: Dalam kehidupan sehari-hari, ia bisa menjadi Obeah man atau bahkan orang terpelajar yang hidup tenang dan menyendiri [lagahoo-c10], tetapi ia ahli melukai atau membunuh [lagahoo-c11]. Untuk melihatnya dengan jelas, orang harus mengoleskan lendir dari mata anjing ke matanya dan mengintip lewat lubang kunci pada tengah malam [lagahoo-c09]. Untuk membunuhnya, ia harus dipukuli dengan tongkat yang diurapi air suci dan minyak suci selama sembilan hari [lagahoo-c06].
long_description.en: In everyday life it could be an Obeah man or even a learned man living a quiet, solitary life [lagahoo-c10], yet it was a genius at maiming or killing [lagahoo-c11]. To see it properly one had to put mucus from a dog's eye in one's own eye and look through a keyhole at midnight [lagahoo-c09]. To kill it, one must beat it with a stick anointed with holy water and holy oil for nine days [lagahoo-c06].

long_description.id: Dalam laporan surat kabar yang dikutip, enam warga memberi tahu polisi bahwa mereka diserang makhluk setengah manusia, setengah kambing, berbulu dan bersisik [lake-worth-monster-c05]. long_description.en: In the newspaper reports quoted, six residents told police they were attacked by a half-man, half-goat creature with fur and scales [lake-worth-monster-c05]. One resident said it leapt from a tree onto his car [lake-worth-monster-c07], and the next night it was said to hurl a tire from a bluff before dozens of witnesses [lake-worth-monster-c08]. Police searched near Greer Island in vain [lake-worth-monster-c06].

long_description.id: Polisi tidak menemukan bukti adanya makhluk itu [lake-worth-monster-c04], dan kehebohan sebagian besar mereda ketika sekolah kembali dibuka [lake-worth-monster-c09]. long_description.en: Police found no evidence of the monster [lake-worth-monster-c04], and the furor largely faded when school resumed [lake-worth-monster-c09]. claims.quote: In Texan folklore, the Lake Worth Monster is a legendary creature said to inhabit Lake Worth at the Fort Worth Nature Center and Refuge, just outside Fort Worth.

statement.en: In Texan folklore, the Lake Worth Monster is a legendary creature said to inhabit Lake Worth near Fort Worth.

claims.quote: The creature is often described as a "part-man, part-goat" with scales and long clawed fingers.

statement.id: Ia sering digambarkan setengah manusia setengah kambing, bersisik, dan berjari panjang bercakar.

claims.quote: Reports of sightings by local citizens of "a half-man, half-goat, with fur and scales" in July 1969 led to the belief that a mysterious creature lived in Lake Worth.

claims.quote: Local police investigated the claims, but found no evidence of the monster in the Lake Worth and Greer Island area.

statement.id: Polisi setempat menyelidikinya tetapi tidak menemukan bukti.

claims.quote: Six terrified residents told police early today they were attacked by a thing they described as being half-man, half-goat and covered with fur and scales.

statement.id: Enam warga melapor kepada polisi bahwa mereka diserang makhluk yang mereka gambarkan setengah manusia, setengah kambing, dan berbulu serta bersisik.
statement.en: Six residents told police they were attacked by a thing they described as half-man, half-goat and covered with fur and scales.

claims.quote: Four units of Fort Worth police and the residents searched in vain for the thing, which was reported seen at Lake Worth, near Greer Island.

statement.id: Empat unit polisi dan para warga mencari makhluk itu tanpa hasil; makhluk itu dilaporkan terlihat di Lake Worth, dekat Greer Island.
statement.en: Four police units and the residents searched in vain for the thing, reported seen at Lake Worth near Greer Island.

claims.quote: John Reichart told police that the creature leapt from a tree and landed on his car, and he showed them an 18-inch scar down the side of his car as proof.

statement.id: Seorang warga mengatakan kepada polisi bahwa makhluk itu melompat dari pohon dan mendarat di mobilnya, dan ia menunjukkan goresan sepanjang 18 inci di sisi mobil sebagai bukti.
statement.en: A resident told police the creature leapt from a tree onto his car, and showed an 18-inch scar down the side of the car as proof.

claims.quote: The next night, the monster, in front of a couple of dozen witnesses, was said to have uttered a "pitiful cry" and hurled a tire from a bluff at them.

statement.id: Pada malam berikutnya, di depan sekitar dua puluh empat saksi, makhluk itu konon mengeluarkan "tangisan memilukan" dan melemparkan ban dari tebing ke arah mereka.
statement.en: The next night, before a couple of dozen witnesses, the monster was said to have uttered a "pitiful cry" and hurled a tire at them from a bluff.

claims.quote: Then, about the time school resumed, perhaps not coincidentally, the Lake Worth Monster furor largely disappeared.

statement.id: Ketika sekolah kembali dibuka, kehebohan tentang Lake Worth Monster sebagian besar mereda.
statement.en: About the time school resumed, the Lake Worth Monster furor largely disappeared.

claims.quote: Or, as more people actually suspect, the monster was really several creatures, all hoaxes carried out by enterprising and opportunistic mischief-makers from Brewer, Castleberry or North Side high school.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, lebih banyak orang menduga "monster" itu sebenarnya beberapa pelaku iseng yang memanfaatkan kesempatan, bukan satu makhluk.
statement.en: The article says more people suspect the monster was really several hoaxes by opportunistic mischief-makers rather than a single creature.

statement.en: Clarke's husband maintains that it was definitely not pranksters.

statement.en: A slightly tongue-in-cheek book, "The Lake Worth Monster of Greer Island," was self-published in September '69.

statement.en: Since 2009, the 40th anniversary of the sightings, the Fort Worth Nature Center and Refuge has held a Lake Worth Monster Bash each October.

short_description.id: Lantern man adalah cahaya hantu dalam folklor The Fens di East Anglia, Inggris, yang dipercaya roh jahat penarik korban ke rawa alang-alang.
short_description.en: A lantern man is a ghost light of the folklore of the Fens of East Anglia, England, believed to be an evil spirit luring victims into the reed beds.

long_description.id: Lantern man adalah cahaya hantu di udara dalam folklor The Fens di East Anglia, dengan penampakan di sekitar Wicken Fen dan daerah lain. Menurut kisah yang pertama dikumpulkan folkloris L. F. Newman, cahaya itu dipercaya roh jahat yang berusaha menarik korban menuju kematian di rawa alang-alang. Roh itu tertarik oleh bunyi siulan, dan cara menghindarinya adalah berbaring telungkup dengan mulut di lumpur. Fenomena ini tampaknya variasi kisah will-o'-the-wisp dan kini dianggap penampakan gas rawa yang terbakar.
long_description.en: A lantern man is an atmospheric ghost light in the folklore of the Fens of East Anglia, reported around Wicken Fen and elsewhere. In stories first gathered by the folklorist L. F. Newman, the lights are wicked spirits trying to lure people to their deaths in the reed beds. Whistling attracts them, and the way to escape is to lie face down with your mouth in the mud. The phenomenon looks like a form of will-o'-the-wisp lore and is now put down to burning marsh gas.

long_description.id: Seorang nelayan setempat bercerita kepada parapsikolog Peter Underwood bahwa ia pernah menjatuhkan diri ke tanah untuk menghindari lantern man yang tertarik oleh siulannya. Seorang lelaki lain yang bersiul memanggil anjingnya di rawa berlindung di rumah temannya, yang menggantungkan sebuah tanduk pada tiang panjang untuk mengalihkan roh itu; paginya tanduk itu ditemukan hangus terbakar.
long_description.en: A local fisherman told the parapsychologist Peter Underwood that he once threw himself flat to escape a lantern man drawn by his whistling. Another man, whistling for his dog on the fen, sheltered at a friend's house; the friend hung a horn on a long pole to distract the spirit, and next morning the horn was found burnt up.

short_description.id: Lava bear adalah beruang hitam kerdil dari dataran lava Oregon yang dulu dikira spesies tersendiri [lava-bear-c01, lava-bear-c03].
short_description.en: The lava bear is a stunted black bear of the Oregon lava beds once thought to be a separate species [lava-bear-c01, lava-bear-c03].

long_description.id: Lava bear adalah variasi beruang hitam Amerika dari dataran lava Oregon [lava-bear-c01], digambarkan sangat kecil dengan bulu cokelat muda [lava-bear-c02]. Beruang itu awalnya disebut sand lapper dan kemudian dikenal sebagai lava bear [lava-bear-c09].
long_description.en: The lava bear is a variety of American black bear from the Oregon lava beds [lava-bear-c01], described as very small with light brown fur [lava-bear-c02]. The bears were initially called sand lappers and later became known as lava bears [lava-bear-c09].

long_description.id: Sejak musim semi 1917 beredar banyak kisah tentang spesies beruang yang belum dikenal [lava-bear-c05]. Seorang penulis pada masa itu mengingat spesimen bernuansa kuning kulit rusa muda dengan bulu seperti wol [lava-bear-c06], yang kemudian dinyatakan sebagai hewan belum dewasa, mungkin spesimen abnormal beruang hitam biasa [lava-bear-c07].
long_description.en: Since the spring of 1917 many tales circulated of a hitherto unknown species of bear [lava-bear-c05]. A writer of the time recalled a specimen with woolly, light buckskin-colored fur [lava-bear-c06], which was then pronounced an immature animal, possibly an abnormal specimen of the common black bear [lava-bear-c07].

long_description.id: Dulu ia dianggap spesies tersendiri, tetapi ilmuwan menyimpulkan hewan itu kerdil karena lingkungannya yang keras [lava-bear-c03], dan kini diterima bahwa lava bear tidak pernah menjadi spesies yang berdiri sendiri [lava-bear-c04]. Meski begitu, para penduduk lama tetap berkeras bahwa beruang kerdil hidup di hamparan lava [lava-bear-c08].
long_description.en: It was once thought to be a separate species, but scientists found the animals stunted by their harsh environment [lava-bear-c03], and it is now accepted that lava bears were never a distinct species [lava-bear-c04]. Even so, old-timers still insist a dwarf bear lives in the lava beds [lava-bear-c08].
