short_description.id: Nagual atau nahual dalam agama rakyat Mesoamerika adalah manusia yang mampu berubah wujud menjadi pasangan hewan tonal-nya, dan dapat memakai kekuatannya untuk kebaikan maupun kejahatan.
short_description.en: In Mesoamerican folk religion a nagual, or nahual, is a person able to shapeshift into his or her animal counterpart, the tonal, and can use that power for good or for evil.

long_description.id: Dalam agama rakyat Mesoamerika, nagual atau nahual adalah manusia yang memiliki kekuatan berubah wujud menjadi pasangan hewan tonal-nya. Kata itu berasal dari kata Nahuatl nāhualli, praktisi agama pribumi yang oleh orang Spanyol disebut 'penyihir'. Sebuah sumber akademik lama mencatat bahwa kata-kata turunan akar na dalam bahasa Nahuatl mengandung gagasan 'mengetahui', dan para misionaris awal menyebut naualli sebagai ahli pengetahuan mistik.
long_description.en: In Mesoamerican folk religion, a nagual or nahual is a person with the power to shapeshift into his or her tonal animal counterpart. The word comes from the Nahuatl nāhualli, an indigenous religious practitioner whom the Spanish called a 'magician'. An older academic source notes that Nahuatl words derived from the root na carry the idea of 'to know', and early missionaries described the naualli as masters of mystic knowledge.

long_description.id: Kebaikan atau kejahatan kekuatan nagual bergantung pada kepribadiannya. Sifat nagual diperoleh sejak lahir bersama ciri lain yang terkait dengan hari kelahiran, dan konsep nagualisme berasal dari Mesoamerika; praktiknya sering disertai halusinogen seperti peyote, dan kepercayaan pada roh pelindung pribadi adalah salah satu doktrin dasarnya. Menurut kutipan dari Sahagún, naualli menakuti orang dan mengisap darah anak-anak pada malam hari, meski ada pula yang memakai seni itu demi kebaikan; yang berniat jahat mencederai korban dan membuat mereka kehilangan akal. Dalam sebuah teks yang dikutip sumber itu, para nanahualtin menghalau awan agar hujan es tidak merusak tanaman, mengubah benda tampak menjadi hewan, dan menjelma menjadi harimau, anjing, musang, burung hantu, atau ayam jantan.
long_description.en: Whether a nagual's power serves good or evil depends on personality. The nagual trait is acquired at birth with other characteristics tied to a person's birth day, and the concept of nagualism is Mesoamerican in origin; its practice was often accompanied by hallucinogens such as peyote, and belief in a personal guardian spirit was one of its fundamental doctrines. According to a passage from Sahagún, the naualli frightens people and sucks children's blood at night, though some use the art only for others' benefit; those with evil intent injure victims and make them lose their reason. In a text quoted by that source, the nanahualtin conjure clouds so hail does not harm crops, make objects look like animals, and take the form of a tiger, dog, weasel, owl, or cock.

long_description.id: Di Meksiko pedesaan modern, nagual kadang disamakan dengan brujo, yang berubah menjadi anjing, burung hantu, kelelawar, serigala, atau kalkun pada malam hari, meminum darah korban, mencuri, dan menimbulkan penyakit. Di sebagian komunitas adat nagual menjadi bagian dari hierarki keagamaan dan dibayar untuk mencabut kutukan nagual lain, sedangkan di komunitas lain, seperti Mixe dan Triqui, mereka yang mengendalikan nahual-nya dihormati sebagai pelindung komunitas. Dewa Tezcatlipoca disebut pelindung nagualisme karena tonal-nya adalah jaguar.
long_description.en: In modern rural Mexico a nagual is sometimes equated with a brujo, who turns into a dog, owl, bat, wolf, or turkey at night, drinks victims' blood, steals, and causes disease. In some indigenous communities the nagual is part of the religious hierarchy and is hired to remove other naguals' curses, while in others, such as the Mixes and Triquis, those who control their nahual are revered as protectors of the community. The god Tezcatlipoca is said to have been the protector of nagualism because his tonal was the jaguar.

cultural_context.id: Di sebagian komunitas adat nagual diintegrasikan ke dalam hierarki keagamaan: komunitas tahu siapa nagual dan menoleransi, menakuti, serta menghormatinya.
cultural_context.en: Some indigenous communities place the nagual within the religious hierarchy, knowing who is one and tolerating, fearing, and respecting them.

literal_meaning.id: praktisi agama pribumi yang oleh orang Spanyol disebut 'penyihir'; akar na berkaitan dengan gagasan 'mengetahui'
literal_meaning.en: an indigenous religious practitioner identified by the Spanish as a 'magician'; the root na carries the idea 'to know'

who.id: Manusia yang mampu berubah wujud menjadi hewan pendampingnya dalam agama rakyat Mesoamerika.
who.en: A human able to shapeshift into his or her animal counterpart in Mesoamerican folk religion.

origin.id: Kepercayaan Mesoamerika dengan akar dalam praktik syaman pra-Kolumbus.
origin.en: A Mesoamerican belief with roots in pre-Columbian shamanistic practice.

role.id: Penyihir atau pelindung komunitas, tergantung pandangan dan kepribadian nagual.
role.en: A sorcerer or a protector of the community, depending on the view and the nagual's personality.

famous_for.id: Kemampuan berubah wujud menjadi hewan dan perannya yang ambivalen dalam komunitas.
famous_for.en: The ability to turn into animals and an ambivalent role in communities.

did_you_know.id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, Tezcatlipoca adalah pelindung nagualisme karena tonal-nya adalah jaguar.
did_you_know.en: Aztec myth made Tezcatlipoca the patron of nagualism, since his tonal was the jaguar.

description.id: Nagual dapat berubah wujud menjadi pasangan hewan tonal-nya; di Meksiko modern biasanya anjing, burung hantu, kelelawar, serigala, atau kalkun.
description.en: A nagual can shapeshift into the tonal animal counterpart; in modern Mexico normally a dog, owl, bat, wolf, or turkey.

description.id: Nagualli dibayar untuk mencabut kutukan yang dilontarkan nagualli lain.
description.en: Nagualli are hired to remove curses cast by other nagualli.

description.id: Para nanahualtin menghalau awan saat ada bahaya hujan es dan membuat tongkat tampak seperti ular atau batu tampak seperti kalajengking.
description.en: The nanahualtin conjure clouds when there is danger of hail and make a stick look like a serpent or a stone like a scorpion.

description.id: Nagual jahat disebut mengisap darah korban dan menimbulkan penyakit.
description.en: An evil nagual is said to drink blood from victims and cause disease.

description.id: Kepercayaan pada nagual sebagai penyihir jahat pengubah wujud lazim di kalangan penduduk adat dan mestizo.
description.en: Belief in naguals as evil shape-shifting witches is common among indigenous and Mestizo populations.

description.id: Mereka yang mengendalikan nahual-nya adalah pelindung masyarakat, sumber daya alam, dan budaya komunitas, sangat dihormati tetapi juga ditakuti.
description.en: Those who master their nahual guard the people, natural resources and culture of the community, and are deeply revered yet also feared.

note.id: Pelindung nagualisme dalam mitologi Aztec karena tonal-nya adalah jaguar.
note.en: The protector of nagualism in Aztec mythology because his tonal was the jaguar.

note.id: Pasangan hewan yang menjadi wujud nagual dan terkait kehidupan seseorang.
note.en: The animal counterpart into which a nagual shifts, to which a person's life force is linked.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa nagual dapat dipandang sebagai pelindung sekaligus ancaman bagi komunitasnya?
learning_questions.en: Why can a nagual be seen both as a protector and a threat to the community?

sources.title: Nagualism: A Study in Native American Folk-lore and History
sources.author: Daniel G. Brinton

claims.quote: Naguals use their powers for good or evil according to their personality.

statement.id: Nagual menggunakan kekuatan mereka untuk kebaikan atau kejahatan sesuai kepribadiannya.
statement.en: Naguals use their powers for good or evil according to their personality.

claims.quote: The general concept of nagualism is Mesoamerican in origin.

statement.id: Konsep umum mengenai nagualisme berakar dari Mesoamerican.
statement.en: The general concept of nagualism is Mesoamerican in origin.

claims.quote: Nagualism is linked with pre-Columbian shamanistic practices through Pre-classic Olmec and Toltec depictions that are interpreted as human beings transforming themselves into animals.

statement.id: Nagualisme terhubung dengan praktik perdukunan Olmec dan Toltec mengenai manusia yang berubah menjadi hewan.
statement.en: Nagualism is linked with pre-Columbian shamanistic practices through Pre-classic Olmec and Toltec depictions that are interpreted as human beings transforming themselves into animals.

claims.quote: Mesoamerican belief in tonalism, wherein every person has an animal counterpart to which their life force is linked, is drawn upon by nagualism.

statement.id: Keyakinan tonalism bahwa setiap orang memiliki padanan hewani menjadi dasar nagualisme.
statement.en: Mesoamerican belief in tonalism, wherein every person has an animal counterpart to which their life force is linked, is drawn upon by nagualism.

claims.quote: In Mesoamerican folk religion, a nagual or nahual (both from the Nahuatl word nāhualli ... is a human being who has the power to shapeshift into their tonal animal counterpart.

statement.id: Dalam agama rakyat Mesoamerika, nagual atau nahual (keduanya dari kata Nahuatl nāhualli) adalah manusia yang memiliki kekuatan berubah wujud menjadi pasangan hewan tonal-nya.
statement.en: In Mesoamerican folk religion, a nagual or nahual (both from the Nahuatl word nāhualli) is a human being who has the power to shapeshift into their tonal animal counterpart.

claims.quote: The word nagual derives from the Nahuatl word nāhualli ... an indigenous religious practitioner, identified by the Spanish as a 'magician'.

statement.id: Kata nagual berasal dari kata Nahuatl nāhualli, seorang praktisi agama pribumi yang oleh orang Spanyol diidentifikasi sebagai 'penyihir'.
statement.en: The word nagual derives from the Nahuatl word nāhualli, an indigenous religious practitioner identified by the Spanish as a 'magician'.

claims.quote: In modern rural Mexico, nagual is sometimes synonymous with brujo ("wizard"); one who is able to shapeshift into an animal at night (normally into a dog, owl, bat, wolf or turkey), drink blood from human victims, steal property, cause disease, and the like.

statement.id: Di Meksiko pedesaan modern, nagual kadang sinonim dengan brujo ('penyihir'): orang yang dapat berubah wujud menjadi hewan pada malam hari (biasanya anjing, burung hantu, kelelawar, serigala, atau kalkun), meminum darah korban manusia, mencuri harta, menimbulkan penyakit, dan sejenisnya.
statement.en: In modern rural Mexico, nagual is sometimes synonymous with brujo ('wizard'): one who can shapeshift into an animal at night (normally a dog, owl, bat, wolf or turkey), drink blood from human victims, steal property, cause disease, and the like.

claims.quote: In some indigenous communities the nagual is integrated into the religious hierarchy. The community knows who is a nagual, tolerating, fearing and respecting them. Nagualli are hired to remove curses cast by other nagualli.

statement.id: Di sebagian komunitas adat, nagual diintegrasikan ke dalam hierarki keagamaan; komunitas tahu siapa nagual, menoleransi, menakuti, dan menghormatinya, dan nagualli dibayar untuk mencabut kutukan yang dilontarkan nagualli lain.
statement.en: In some indigenous communities the nagual is integrated into the religious hierarchy; the community knows who is a nagual, tolerating, fearing and respecting them, and nagualli are hired to remove curses cast by other nagualli.

claims.quote: In Aztec mythology the god Tezcatlipoca was the protector of nagualism, because his tonal was the jaguar and he governed the distribution of wealth.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, dewa Tezcatlipoca adalah pelindung nagualisme, karena tonal-nya adalah jaguar dan ia mengatur pembagian kekayaan.
statement.en: In Aztec mythology the god Tezcatlipoca was the protector of nagualism, because his tonal was the jaguar and he governed the distribution of wealth.

claims.quote: The nagual trait is acquired at birth, along with other characteristics associated with a person's birth day.

statement.id: Sifat nagual diperoleh sejak lahir, bersama ciri lain yang terkait dengan hari kelahiran seseorang.
statement.en: The nagual trait is acquired at birth, along with other characteristics associated with a person's birth day.

claims.quote: Kaplan concludes that, in Oaxaca, the belief in naguals as evil, shape shifting witches is common in both indigenous and Mestizo populations. According to Kaplan, the belief in animal spirit companions is exclusively indigenous.

statement.id: Kaplan menyimpulkan bahwa di Oaxaca kepercayaan pada nagual sebagai penyihir jahat pengubah wujud lazim di kalangan penduduk adat dan mestizo, sedangkan kepercayaan pada pendamping roh hewan menurutnya eksklusif milik masyarakat adat.
statement.en: Kaplan concludes that in Oaxaca the belief in naguals as evil shape-shifting witches is common among both indigenous and Mestizo populations, while the belief in animal spirit companions is exclusively indigenous.

claims.quote: This is certain for some groups and communities, but for others, such as the Mixes, Chinantecos, Triquis, or Tacuates, those who can control their nahual or alterego are protectors of the people, natural resources and culture of the community, highly revered, but also feared.

statement.id: Bagi sebagian kelompok seperti Mixe, Chinanteco, Triqui, atau Tacuate, mereka yang dapat mengendalikan nahual atau alter ego-nya adalah pelindung masyarakat, sumber daya alam, dan budaya komunitas, sangat dihormati tetapi juga ditakuti.
statement.en: For some groups such as the Mixes, Chinantecos, Triquis, or Tacuates, those who can control their nahual or alterego are protectors of the people, natural resources and culture of the community, highly revered but also feared.

claims.quote: The practice of Nagualism was often accompanied by use of hallucinogens, including peyote, ololiuqui, and psylocibin mushrooms known as teonanácatl.

statement.id: Praktik nagualisme sering disertai pemakaian halusinogen, termasuk peyote, ololiuqui, dan jamur psilosibin yang dikenal sebagai teonanácatl.
statement.en: The practice of Nagualism was often accompanied by use of hallucinogens, including peyote, ololiuqui, and psylocibin mushrooms known as teonanácatl.

claims.quote: The early missionaries to New Spain often speak of the naualli (plural, nanahualtin), masters of mystic knowledge, dealers in the black art, wizards or sorcerers. They were not always evil-minded persons, though they seem to have been generally feared.

statement.id: Para misionaris awal di Spanyol Baru sering menyebut naualli (jamak nanahualtin), ahli pengetahuan mistik, pelaku ilmu hitam, penyihir; mereka tidak selalu berniat jahat, meski tampaknya umumnya ditakuti.
statement.en: The early missionaries to New Spain often speak of the naualli (plural nanahualtin), masters of mystic knowledge, dealers in the black art, wizards or sorcerers; they were not always evil-minded, though they seem to have been generally feared.

claims.quote: The earliest source of information about them is Father Sahagun, who, in his invaluable History, has the following paragraph: ... “The naualli, or magician, is he who frightens men and sucks the blood of children during the night. He is well skilled in the practice of this trade, he knows all the arts of sorcery (nauallotl) and employs them with cunning and ability;

statement.id: Dalam kutipan dari Sahagún, naualli atau penyihir adalah orang yang menakuti manusia dan mengisap darah anak-anak pada malam hari; ia mahir dalam kerja ini, menguasai semua seni sihir (nauallotl), dan memakainya dengan cerdik dan cakap.
statement.en: In a quotation from Sahagún, the naualli, or magician, is he who frightens men and sucks the blood of children during the night; he is well skilled in this trade, knows all the arts of sorcery (nauallotl), and employs them with cunning and ability.

claims.quote: Those who have recourse to such arts for evil intents injure the bodies of their victims, cause them to lose their reason and smother them. These are wicked men and necromancers.

statement.id: Mereka yang memakai seni semacam itu untuk maksud jahat mencederai tubuh korban, membuat mereka kehilangan akal, dan mencekik mereka; mereka adalah orang jahat dan pemanggil arwah.
statement.en: Those who have recourse to such arts for evil intents injure the bodies of their victims, cause them to lose their reason and smother them; these are wicked men and necromancers.

claims.quote: nanahualtin, who conjure the clouds when there is danger of hail, so that the crops may not be injured. They can also make a stick look like a serpent, a mat like a centipede, a piece of stone like a scorpion, and similar deceptions.

statement.id: Menurut kutipan itu, para nanahualtin menghalau awan ketika ada bahaya hujan es agar tanaman tidak rusak, dan dapat membuat tongkat tampak seperti ular, tikar seperti lipan, dan batu seperti kalajengking.
statement.en: According to the quoted instruction, the nanahualtin conjure the clouds when there is danger of hail so the crops are not injured, and can make a stick look like a serpent, a mat like a centipede, and a piece of stone like a scorpion.

claims.quote: Others of these nanahualtin will transform themselves to all appearances (segun la aparencia), into a tiger, a dog or a weasel. Others again will take the form of an owl, a cock, or a weasel;

statement.id: Nanahualtin lain, menurut kutipan itu, mengubah diri secara kasatmata menjadi harimau, anjing, atau musang; yang lain mengambil rupa burung hantu, ayam jantan, atau musang.
statement.en: Others of the nanahualtin, according to the quotation, transform themselves in appearance into a tiger, a dog or a weasel, and others take the form of an owl, a cock, or a weasel.

claims.quote: The belief in a personal guardian spirit was one of the fundamental doctrines of Nagualism ... By consulting it the appropriate nagual was discovered and assigned, and this was certainly a prominent feature in the native cult and has never been abandoned.

statement.id: Kepercayaan pada roh pelindung pribadi adalah salah satu doktrin dasar nagualisme; dengan berkonsultasi pada kalender, nagual yang sesuai ditemukan dan ditetapkan, dan ini merupakan ciri menonjol dalam kultus pribumi yang tak pernah ditinggalkan.
statement.en: The belief in a personal guardian spirit was one of the fundamental doctrines of Nagualism; by consulting the calendar the appropriate nagual was discovered and assigned, a prominent feature of the native cult that has never been abandoned.

claims.quote: We do find, however, in the Nahuatl language ... a number of derivatives from the same root, na, among them this very word, Nahuatl, all of them containing the idea “to know,” or “knowledge.”

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Nahuatl terdapat sejumlah turunan dari akar yang sama, na, termasuk kata Nahuatl itu sendiri, yang semuanya mengandung gagasan 'mengetahui' atau 'pengetahuan'.
statement.en: In the Nahuatl language there are a number of derivatives from the same root, na, among them the word Nahuatl itself, all of them containing the idea 'to know' or 'knowledge'.

long_description.id: Nain Rouge adalah makhluk legenda Detroit yang kemunculannya konon menandakan kemalangan [nain-rouge-c01], juga disebut "Iblis dari Selat" [nain-rouge-c04]. Menurut kisahnya, pendiri Detroit, Cadillac, memukulnya dengan tongkat alih-alih menenangkannya [nain-rouge-c03]. Tidak ada catatan legenda ini sebelum tahun 1880-an [nain-rouge-c02].
long_description.en: The Nain Rouge is a Detroit legendary creature whose appearance presages misfortune [nain-rouge-c01], also called "the Demon of the Strait" [nain-rouge-c04]. In the tale, founder Cadillac struck it with his cane instead of appeasing it [nain-rouge-c03]. No records of the legend predate the 1880s [nain-rouge-c02].

long_description.id: Dalam teks koleksi legenda yang dikutip, ia digambarkan sebagai sosok kerdil yang kasar, sangat merah wajahnya, bermata cerah berkilau [nain-rouge-c06], dengan mulut menyeringai berisi gigi tajam dan runcing [nain-rouge-c07]. Sebuah catatan kaki menyebutnya iblis dari Selat yang sangat jahat jika tersinggung tetapi bisa ditenangkan dengan sanjungan [nain-rouge-c08]. Ketika ia lenyap, terdengar tawa jahat yang mengejek [nain-rouge-c09].
long_description.en: In the legend collection quoted, it is described as an uncouth dwarf, very red in the face, with a bright, glistening eye [nain-rouge-c06], and a grinning mouth of sharp, pointed teeth [nain-rouge-c07]. A footnote calls it the demon of the Strait, most malignant if offended but capable of being appeased by flattery [nain-rouge-c08]. As it vanished, a fiendish, mocking laugh was heard [nain-rouge-c09].

long_description.id: Teks yang sama menyebut kemunculannya sebagai pertanda pasti malapetaka [nain-rouge-c10], dan ia konon terlihat berlari di sepanjang pantai pada malam sebelum serangan nahas di Bloody Run [nain-rouge-c11]. Kini setiap musim semi diadakan Marche du Nain Rouge [nain-rouge-c05].
long_description.en: The same text calls its appearance a sure sign of impending evil [nain-rouge-c10], and it was said to be seen running along the shore the night before the ill-fated attack at Bloody Run [nain-rouge-c11]. Each spring the Marche du Nain Rouge is held [nain-rouge-c05].

short_description.id: Beruang Nandi adalah kriptid dari Afrika Timur yang dinamai menurut orang Nandi di Kenya barat; ia digambarkan sebagai pemangsa malam yang ganas, tetapi para ilmuwan meragukan keberadaannya.
short_description.en: The Nandi bear is a cryptid from East Africa named after the Nandi people of western Kenya; it is pictured as a fierce night-time predator, though scientists doubt that it exists.

long_description.id: Beruang Nandi adalah kriptid yang konon hidup di Afrika Timur. Namanya berasal dari orang Nandi di Kenya barat, wilayah tempat makhluk ini dilaporkan, dan ia juga disebut chemosit, chimiset, kerit, chimit, kikambungure, duba, atau sabroukoo. Nkampit dari orang Samburu tampaknya merupakan versi makhluk yang sama.
long_description.en: The Nandi bear is a cryptid said to live in East Africa. It owes its name to the Nandi people of western Kenya, where sightings were reported, and it also goes by chemosit, chimiset, kerit, chimit, kikambungure, duba or sabroukoo. The Nkampit of the Samburu seems to be another form of the same creature.

long_description.id: Penggambarannya adalah karnivora ganas bertubuh kuat dengan bahu depan tinggi. Menurut cerita yang saling cocok, hewan ini cukup besar, kadang berdiri dengan kaki belakang, aktif di malam hari, dan membunuh manusia maupun hewan. Legenda setempat menambahkan bulu kemerahan, kaki panjang, kebiasaan menguliti kepala korban, bahkan hanya memakan otaknya.
long_description.en: It is portrayed as a savage, heavily built meat-eater whose front shoulders stand high. The stories that agree make it a fairly large beast that sometimes rears on its hind legs, roams at night and kills both people and animals. Local legend adds reddish fur and long feet, says it scalps people, and even claims it eats nothing but the brain of its victims.

long_description.id: Sebuah tulisan dalam jurnal sejarah alam menyebut chemosit di antara hewan aneh yang dilaporkan dari British East Africa. Penulisnya hanya tahu satu kisah tentang hewan itu dibunuh, yaitu dari distrik Maraquet: sekelompok pria memasang boneka manusia di ambang pintu pondok dan menunggu di dalam sampai hewan itu datang. Ia menilai kisah-kisah di kalangan penduduk setempat setengah legenda dan tetap hidup karena kematian orang atau ternak yang tidak biasa, meski hewan itu punya nama lokal dan dikenal luas di kalangan orang Nandi.
long_description.en: A natural history journal paper lists the chemosit among the odd animals reported from British East Africa. Its author knew of only one tale of the beast being killed, from the Maraquet district: a group of men set a dummy man in a hut doorway and waited inside for the animal to come. He judged the local stories to be partly legend, sustained by unusual deaths of people or cattle, while noting that the creature had a native name and was widely known among the Nandi.

long_description.id: Para ilmuwan cenderung meragukan keberadaannya dan menganggap laporannya sebagai salah tafsir atas hewan yang sudah dikenal. Zoolog Reginald Innes Pocock mengaitkannya dengan dubuk tutul, sebagian orang menduga dubuk raksasa dari zaman es, dan pada 1930-an Louis Leakey membandingkannya dengan Chalicothere. Penulis jurnal tadi berpendapat chimiset sebenarnya gabungan dari sejumlah hewan.
long_description.en: Scientists generally doubt that it exists and treat the reports as known animals misread. Zoologist Reginald Innes Pocock linked it to the spotted hyena, others have proposed a giant ice-age hyena, and in the 1930s Louis Leakey compared it with the Chalicothere. The journal author mentioned above thought the chimiset was really a blend of several different animals.

cultural_context.id: Seorang penulis awal menilai kisah chemosit di kalangan penduduk setempat setengah legenda, yang terus hidup setiap kali ada orang atau ternak terbunuh dengan cara tidak biasa.
cultural_context.en: An early writer judged local chemosit stories to be half legendary, kept alive whenever people or cattle were killed in an unusual way.

short_description.id: Nian adalah makhluk dalam kisah Tiongkok yang tinggal di laut atau gunung.
short_description.en: Nian is a beast in Chinese tales said to inhabit the sea or mountains.

long_description.id: Nian adalah makhluk dalam kisah Tiongkok yang tinggal di laut atau gunung. Catatan tertulis tentang Nian sebagai makhluk baru diketahui dari awal abad kedua puluh.
long_description.en: Nian is a beast in Chinese tales said to inhabit the sea or mountains. The earliest written sources describing Nian as a creature date from the early 20th century.

long_description.id: Kisah menyebutnya keluar pada tahun baru untuk memangsa manusia dan hewan. Penampilan Nian memiliki varian, termasuk singa berwajah datar dengan tubuh anjing. Legenda menjelaskan pemasangan lentera merah sebagai upaya menghindari serangan Nian. Praktik perayaan lebih dahulu tercatat dalam teks kuno tanpa menyebut makhluk bernama Nian.
long_description.en: The tale describes it emerging at New Year to feed on people and animals. Nian's appearance varies, including a flat-faced lion with a dog's body. A legend explains red lanterns as an attempt to avert Nian's attacks. Celebration practices were recorded in ancient texts without mentioning a creature named Nian.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda yang dimuat portal china.org.cn, Nian adalah monster bertanduk yang tinggal di dasar laut dan naik ke pantai pada malam tahun baru untuk melahap ternak dan membunuh orang. Penduduk desa mengungsi ke pegunungan setiap malam itu. Dalam kisah tersebut, seorang pengemis tua mengusirnya dengan memanfaatkan hal yang paling ditakuti Nian, yaitu warna merah, api, dan ledakan, dan penduduk kemudian memakai kertas merah serta petasan untuk menolak monster itu.
long_description.en: According to a legend published on china.org.cn, Nian is a horned monster living at the bottom of the sea that climbs ashore on New Year's Eve to devour cattle and kill people. Villagers fled to the mountains every such night. In the story an old beggar drives it off by using what Nian fears most, the color red, flames and explosions, and the villagers afterward used red paper and firecrackers to repel the monster.

literal_meaning.id: Aksara nian lebih sering berarti "tahun" atau "tahun baru".
literal_meaning.en: The Chinese character nian more usually means "year" or "new year".

title.en: The legend of Nian and the old beggar

role.id: Monster yang takut pada merah, api, dan ledakan
role.en: The monster that fears red, flames and explosions

summary.id: Setiap malam tahun baru penduduk mengungsi ke gunung. Suatu tahun seorang pengemis tua berjanji mengusir Nian; rumah sang nenek ditempeli kertas merah, lalu terdengar ledakan, dan Nian lari ketakutan. Penduduk lalu menganggap benda merah dan petasan sebagai penolak monster.
summary.en: Every New Year's Eve people fled to the mountains. One year an old beggar promised to drive Nian away; the grandmother's house was covered in red paper, explosions sounded, and Nian fled in fear. The villagers came to regard red items and firecrackers as ways of driving the monster off.

claims.quote: A nian beast (traditional Chinese: 年獸; simplified Chinese: 年兽; Hanyu Pinyin: Nián shòu; Tongyong Pinyin: Nián shòu; Wade–Giles: Nien2 shou4; Cantonese Yale: Nìhn sau; Zhuyin Fuhao: ㄋㄧㄢˊ ㄕㄡˋ) is a beast in Chinese mythology. According to Chinese mythology, the nian lives under the sea or in the mountains. The Chinese character nian more usually means "year" or "new year".

statement.id: Nian adalah makhluk dalam kisah Tiongkok yang tinggal di laut atau gunung.
statement.en: Nian is a beast in Chinese tales said to inhabit the sea or mountains.

claims.quote: The earliest written sources that refer to the nian as a creature date to the early 20th century.

statement.id: Catatan tertulis tentang Nian sebagai makhluk baru diketahui dari awal abad kedua puluh.
statement.en: The earliest written sources describing Nian as a creature date from the early 20th century.

claims.quote: Once every year at the beginning of Chinese New Year, the nian would come out of its hiding place to feed, mostly on people and animals. During the winter, when food was scarce, it would raid villages, eating the crops and sometimes the villagers themselves - particularly their children.

statement.id: Kisah menyebutnya keluar pada tahun baru untuk memangsa manusia dan hewan.
statement.en: The tale describes it emerging at New Year to feed on people and animals.

claims.quote: Several accounts describe its appearance, with some claiming that it resembles a flat-faced lion with the body of a dog and prominent incisors.

statement.id: Penampilan Nian memiliki varian, termasuk singa berwajah datar dengan tubuh anjing.
statement.en: Nian's appearance varies, including a flat-faced lion with a dog's body.

claims.quote: Some local legends attribute the Chinese lion dance (舞獅) to the nian. The tradition has its origins in a story of a nian's attack on a village. After the attack, the villagers discussed how to make the nian leave them in peace. Since it was discovered that the beast was afraid of the color red, people put red lanterns and spring scrolls on their windows and doors.

statement.id: Legenda menjelaskan pemasangan lentera merah sebagai upaya menghindari serangan Nian.
statement.en: A legend explains red lanterns as an attempt to avert Nian's attacks.

claims.quote: Various aspects of cultural practices relating to Chinese New Year are part of the nian legend. These cultural practices are recorded in ancient texts, though none of them refer to a creature called nian.

statement.id: Praktik perayaan lebih dahulu tercatat dalam teks kuno tanpa menyebut makhluk bernama Nian.
statement.en: Celebration practices were recorded in ancient texts without mentioning a creature named Nian.

claims.quote: According to one of the most famous legends, in ancient China there lived a horned monster named Nian who was extremely ferocious. Nian lived deep at the bottom of the sea all the year round and climbed up to the shore only on New Year's Eve to devour the cattle and kill people.
claims.locator: Bagian legenda asal Festival Musim Semi

statement.id: Menurut salah satu legenda paling terkenal, di Tiongkok kuno hidup monster bertanduk bernama Nian yang sangat garang; ia tinggal jauh di dasar laut sepanjang tahun dan naik ke pantai hanya pada malam tahun baru untuk melahap ternak dan membunuh orang.
statement.en: According to one of the most famous legends, an extremely ferocious horned monster named Nian lived in ancient China, deep at the bottom of the sea all year, and climbed up to the shore only on New Year's Eve to devour cattle and kill people.

claims.quote: Thereupon on the day of every New Year's Eve people from all villages would flee, bringing along the old and the young, to the remote mountains so as to avoid the calamity caused by the monster Nian.
claims.locator: Bagian legenda asal Festival Musim Semi

statement.id: Setiap malam tahun baru, penduduk semua desa mengungsi bersama kaum tua dan muda ke pegunungan terpencil untuk menghindari bencana yang ditimbulkan monster Nian.
statement.en: On every New Year's Eve, people from all villages would flee with the old and the young to the remote mountains to avoid the calamity caused by the monster Nian.

claims.quote: It turned out that the color red, flames, and explosions were what Nian feared the most.
claims.locator: Bagian legenda asal Festival Musim Semi

statement.id: Dalam legenda ini, warna merah, api, dan ledakan adalah hal yang paling ditakuti Nian.
statement.en: In this legend, the color red, flames and explosions were what Nian feared the most.

claims.quote: And when the door of the grandmother's house was thrown open and an old man in a red robe burst out laughing in the courtyard, the monster Nian was scared out of his wits and fled helter-skelter.
claims.locator: Bagian legenda asal Festival Musim Semi

statement.id: Ketika pintu rumah sang nenek dibuka dan seorang lelaki tua berjubah merah tertawa terbahak di halaman, monster Nian ketakutan dan lari tunggang langgang.
statement.en: When the door of the grandmother's house was thrown open and an old man in a red robe burst out laughing in the courtyard, the monster Nian was scared out of his wits and fled helter-skelter.

claims.quote: They concluded in the end that the old beggar was surely the celestial being who came to expel the calamities and bless the people, and that red paper, red cloth, red candles, and the exploding firecracker were certainly the magic weapons to drive out the monster Nian.
claims.locator: Bagian legenda asal Festival Musim Semi

statement.id: Penduduk akhirnya menyimpulkan bahwa pengemis tua itu pastilah makhluk langit yang datang mengusir bencana, dan bahwa kertas merah, kain merah, lilin merah, dan petasan adalah senjata ajaib untuk mengusir monster Nian.
statement.en: The villagers concluded that the old beggar was surely a celestial being come to expel calamities, and that red paper, red cloth, red candles and exploding firecrackers were magic weapons to drive out the monster Nian.

short_description.id: Nüba adalah dewi kekeringan dalam mitologi Tiongkok, juga dikenal sebagai Ba atau Hanba.
short_description.en: Nüba is a Chinese drought goddess also called Ba or Hanba.

long_description.id: Nüba adalah dewi kekeringan dalam mitologi Tiongkok, juga dikenal sebagai Ba atau Hanba. Ba adalah nama pribadinya, nü menandai perempuan, dan han berarti kekeringan.
long_description.en: Nüba is a Chinese drought goddess also called Ba or Hanba. Ba is her personal name, nü marks femininity, and han denotes drought.

long_description.id: Ia disebut putri Kaisar Kuning yang membantu pertempuran melawan Chiyou. Ketika Chiyou mengerahkan dewa angin dan dewa hujan, Ba turun dari langit dan memakai kekuatan keringnya untuk mengalahkan kekuatan angin dan hujan itu. Teks Shanhaijing menyebut hujan berhenti setelah Ba diturunkan dan Chiyou terbunuh. Ia juga disebut salah satu dewi paling awal dalam sastra Tiongkok.
long_description.en: She is described as the Yellow Emperor's daughter who helped in the battle against Chiyou. When Chiyou fielded a wind god and a rain god, Ba descended from heaven and used her drought power to defeat their wind and rain powers. The Shanhaijing text says the rain stopped once Ba was sent down and Chiyou was killed. She is also described as one of the first goddesses in Chinese literature.

long_description.id: Setelah itu Ba tidak dapat naik kembali, dan tempat tinggalnya tidak turun hujan. Ia kemudian mengembara ke bagian utara bumi dan kekeringan terjadi di mana pun ia muncul. Shanhaijing menambahkan bahwa ia kemudian ditempatkan di utara Sungai Merah, dan bahwa orang yang ingin mengusirnya memerintahkan "Dewa, pergilah ke utara!" sambil lebih dulu membersihkan saluran air. Upacara pengusiran Ba untuk mendatangkan hujan masih diadakan di banyak daerah hingga pertengahan abad kedua puluh.
long_description.en: After that Ba could not go back up, and no rain fell where she dwelt. She then wandered to the northern parts of the earth and a drought occurred wherever she appeared. The Shanhaijing adds that she was afterwards placed north of the Red River, and that whoever wishes to drive her away commands "Deity, go north!" while first clearing the waterways. Ceremonies to drive Ba out and bring rain were held in many regions of China until the middle of the twentieth century.

long_description.id: Dalam Shanhaijing, Ba digambarkan mengenakan pakaian gelap. Dalam Shenyijing, tingginya sekitar dua sampai tiga chi, selebihnya tampak seperti manusia, dan ia berjalan telanjang secepat angin. Dalam Kitab Han Akhir, Yinglong dihubungkan sebagai pendampingnya dan keduanya bertempur melawan pasukan Chiyou.
long_description.en: In the Shanhaijing, Ba is described as dressed in dark clothes. In the Shenyijing she is about two to three chis tall, otherwise looking like a person, and walked naked as fast as the wind. In the Book of the Later Han, Yinglong was connected as her companion and they fought against Chiyou's forces.

description.id: Ba menggunakan kekuatan keringnya untuk mengalahkan kekuatan angin dan hujan yang dikerahkan Chiyou; di tempat tinggalnya tidak turun hujan.
description.en: Ba used her drought power to defeat the wind and rain powers fielded by Chiyou; no rain fell where she dwelt.

description.id: Upacara pengusiran Ba dimaksudkan mengakhiri kekeringan karena kekeringan dianggap pergi bersamanya; Shanhaijing juga menyebut perintah "Dewa, pergilah ke utara!" bagi yang ingin mengusirnya.
description.en: Ceremonies to drive Ba out were meant to end drought because the drought was thought to depart with her; the Shanhaijing also gives the command "Deity, go north!" for those who wish to drive her away.

role.id: Dewi kekeringan yang membantu Kaisar Kuning.
role.en: Drought deity who helped the Yellow Emperor.

summary.id: Ketika Chiyou mengerahkan dewa angin dan dewa hujan, Ba turun dari langit dan memakai kekuatan keringnya untuk mengalahkan kekuatan mereka.
summary.en: When Chiyou fielded a wind god and a rain god, Ba descended from heaven and used her drought power to defeat their powers.

statement.en: This text mentions a person in dark-blue clothes named Ba, daughter of the Yellow Emperor; Chiyou attacked the Yellow Emperor, Yinglong held back water, Chiyou summoned the Wind Earl and Rain Master who unleashed a great storm, then the Yellow Emperor sent down the heavenly woman named Ba, the rain stopped, and Chiyou was killed.

claims.quote: 魃不得復上，所居不雨。叔均言之帝，後置之赤水之北。叔均乃為田祖。

statement.en: The text says Ba could not go back up and no rain fell where she dwelt; Shu Jun told the emperor, Ba was afterwards placed north of the Red River, and Shu Jun became the ancestor of the fields (tianzu).

claims.quote: 魃時亡之，所欲逐之者，令曰：「神北行！」先除水道，决通溝瀆。

statement.en: The text adds that whoever wishes to drive her away commands "Deity, go north!" and first clears the waterways and opens drains and ditches.

claims.quote: After having descended from Heaven to aid Huangdi at Zhuolu, instead of returning to heaven, Ba wandered to the northern parts of the earth. Wherever Ba appeared, there would be a drought.

statement.en: After descending from Heaven to aid Huangdi at Zhuolu, Ba did not return to heaven but wandered to the northern parts of the earth; wherever she appeared there was a drought.

claims.quote: In the Book of the Later Han, Yinglong was connected as a companion to Nüba in the myth. They fought simultaneously against Chiyou's forces.

statement.id: Dalam Kitab Han Akhir, Yinglong dihubungkan sebagai pendamping Nüba dalam mitos itu, dan keduanya bertempur bersamaan melawan pasukan Chiyou.
statement.en: In the Book of the Later Han, Yinglong was connected as a companion to Nüba in the myth, and they fought simultaneously against Chiyou's forces.

short_description.id: Okuri-suzume adalah yōkai dari Wakayama dan Nara yang berkicau mengikuti pejalan di jalan gunung malam hari. Dikatakan serigala menyusul setelah kicauannya.
short_description.en: The okuri-suzume is a yōkai of Wakayama and Nara that follows walkers chirping on mountain paths at night. Wolves are said to follow after its call.

long_description.id: Okuri-suzume (送り雀) adalah yōkai yang dikisahkan di Wakayama dan di Desa Higashiyoshino, Distrik Yoshino, Nara. Di Wakayama ia juga disebut suzume-okuri, dan kicauannya diibaratkan burung aoji sehingga ia disebut pula 蒿雀.
long_description.en: The okuri-suzume (送り雀) is a yōkai told of in Wakayama and in Higashiyoshino Village, Yoshino District, Nara. In Wakayama it is also called suzume-okuri, and its call is likened to the real bird aoji, so it is also called 蒿雀.

long_description.id: Ketika orang berjalan di jalan gunung malam hari, ia terbang mendekat sambil berkicau; ia juga dikatakan mendekat saat orang berjalan dengan lentera, dan di Wakayama sering muncul di Gunung Myōhō. Setelah kicauan itu dikatakan muncul serigala atau yōkai okuri-ōkami yang menyerang orang yang jatuh, sehingga orang berjalan sambil memperhatikan langkah. Satu ringkasan basis data Nichibunken justru menyebutnya tidak berbuat jahat.
long_description.en: When people walk mountain paths at night, it flies near chirping; it is also said to come near when someone walks with a lantern, and in Wakayama it often appeared on Mount Myōhō. After the call, wolves or the okuri-ōkami yōkai are said to appear and attack anyone who falls, so people walked watching their footing. One Nichibunken database summary instead says it does no harm.

long_description.id: Sesuai namanya ia dianggap berwujud burung, tetapi tak seorang pun melihatnya; sebagian menyebutnya aoji, yang lain menunjuk bahwa ia terbang malam sehingga berbeda, dan di sebagian daerah dikatakan kelinci. Yōkai serupa adalah yosuzume, yang di Nara kadang disamakan dengan okuri-suzume.
long_description.en: As the name suggests it is said to be bird-shaped, yet no one has seen it; some call it the aoji, others note it flies at night and so differs, and in some regions it is said to be a hare. A similar yōkai is the yosuzume, which in Nara is sometimes identified with the okuri-suzume.

claims.quote: 送り雀（おくりすずめ）は、和歌山県や奈良県吉野郡東吉野村に伝わる妖怪。和歌山では雀送り（すずめおくり）ともいう。

statement.id: Okuri-suzume adalah yōkai yang dikisahkan di Prefektur Wakayama dan di Desa Higashiyoshino, Distrik Yoshino, Prefektur Nara.
statement.en: Okuri-suzume is a yōkai known in Wakayama Prefecture and in Higashiyoshino Village, Yoshino District, Nara Prefecture.

claims.quote: 和歌山では雀送り（すずめおくり）ともいう。その鳴き声を実在の鳥のアオジにたとえ、蒿雀（あおじ）とも呼ばれる。

statement.id: Wakayama juga memakai nama suzume-okuri.
statement.en: Wakayama also uses the name suzume-okuri.

claims.quote: 夜、人が山道を歩いていると「チチチチ……」と鳴きながら飛んでくる。夜に提灯を灯して歩いていると、寄って来るともいう。

statement.id: Ia mendekati orang yang berjalan di jalur pegunungan malam hari sambil bersuara.
statement.en: It approaches people walking mountain paths at night while calling.

claims.quote: この鳴き声の後にはオオカミ、もしくは妖怪・送り狼が現れるといい、道で転倒するとすぐにそれらに襲撃されてしまうため、送り雀の鳴き声を聞いた者は、転ばないよう足元に注意を払いつつ歩いたという。

statement.id: Suaranya konon mendahului serigala atau okuri-ōkami.
statement.en: Its call is said to precede wolves or an okuri-ōkami.

claims.quote: 雀の名の通り、鳥の姿だとされるが、その姿を見た者は誰もいない。前述のアオジが送り雀の正体ともいうが、夜に飛ぶためにアオジとは違うとの指摘もあり、実は兎だという地域もある。

statement.id: Sesuai namanya ia dianggap berwujud burung, tetapi tak seorang pun pernah melihat wujudnya; ada yang menyebut wujud aslinya aoji (burung nyata), ada yang menunjuk bahwa ia terbang malam sehingga berbeda dari aoji, dan di sebagian daerah dikatakan sebenarnya kelinci.
statement.en: As the name suggests it is said to be bird-shaped, yet no one has seen its form; some say its true identity is the aoji (a real bird), others note it flies at night and so differs from the aoji, and in some regions it is said to be a hare.

claims.quote: また、これと似た妖怪に「夜雀」があり、奈良では夜雀が送り雀と同一視されることもある。

statement.id: Yōkai serupa adalah yosuzume ("burung pipit malam"); di Nara, yosuzume kadang disamakan dengan okuri-suzume.
statement.en: A similar yōkai is the yosuzume ("night sparrow"); in Nara the yosuzume is sometimes identified with the okuri-suzume.

claims.quote: 夜に提灯を灯して歩いていると、寄って来るともいう。和歌山では妙法山によく現れたという。

statement.id: Dikatakan ia mendekat ketika orang berjalan dengan lentera di malam hari, dan di Wakayama sering muncul di Gunung Myōhō.
statement.en: It is also said to come near when someone walks at night carrying a lantern, and in Wakayama it often appeared on Mount Myōhō.

claims.quote: 地域（都道府県名） 奈良県 ■ 地域（市・郡名） 五條市 ■ 地域（区町村名） 大塔町 ■ 要約 夜雀というのがいた。夜に、ちっち、ちっちと鳴き、ついて来た。それが送り雀だということを聞いたことがある。

statement.id: Ringkasan dalam basis data tradisi yōkai Nichibunken untuk kasus di Prefektur Nara (Gojō, Ōto) menyebut ada "yosuzume" yang berkicau "chitchi, chitchi" di malam hari dan mengikuti orang, dan si pencerita pernah mendengar itu disebut okuri-suzume.
statement.en: A summary in the Nichibunken yōkai tradition database for a case in Nara Prefecture (Gojō, Ōto) says there was a "night sparrow" that chirped "chitchi, chitchi" at night and followed people, and the teller had heard it called okuri-suzume.

claims.quote: 晩方、送り雀がチンチンと鳴き声をさせてついてくるが、悪いことはしない。

statement.id: Satu ringkasan dalam basis data Nichibunken menyebut okuri-suzume mengikuti sambil berkicau "chinchin" menjelang malam tetapi tidak berbuat jahat.
statement.en: One summary in the Nichibunken database says the okuri-suzume follows at dusk chirping "chinchin" but does no harm.

claims.quote: オクリスズメは夜の山道でちちちちと啼きながら後先を飛ぶ小鳥であるといわれているが、夜に飛ぶので鳥ではない。送雀が鳴くと送狼がついているしらせだといわれる。

statement.id: Satu ringkasan dalam basis data Nichibunken menyebut okuri-suzume terbang bolak-balik di jalan gunung malam hari sambil berkicau, tetapi karena terbang malam ia disebut bukan burung; kicauannya dikatakan pertanda okuri-ōkami (serigala pengantar) ada di dekat.
statement.en: One summary in the Nichibunken database says the okuri-suzume flies back and forth on night mountain paths chirping, but since it flies at night it is said not to be a bird; its call is said to signal that an okuri-ōkami is following.

statement.en: One summary in the Nichibunken database says someone walking at night with a lantern hears chirping "chi, chi, chi" but no one has seen its form; some say a hare, others the aoji, and it is thought not to be a bird.

short_description.id: Orang bunian adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Melayu dan Indonesia yang tak terlihat oleh kebanyakan manusia; namanya berarti orang tersembunyi, dan mereka digambarkan rupawan dan hampir sama dengan manusia.
short_description.en: Orang bunian are supernatural beings of Malay and Indonesian folklore invisible to most humans; the name means hidden people, and they are pictured as beautiful and nearly identical to humans.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Malaysia, Singapura, Brunei, dan Indonesia, orang bunian adalah makhluk gaib yang konon tak terlihat oleh kebanyakan manusia, kecuali yang memiliki penglihatan batin. Istilah ini sering diterjemahkan sebagai peri, tetapi arti harfiahnya orang tersembunyi atau orang bersiul. Mereka digambarkan rupawan, berbusana gaya Asia Tenggara kuno, dan hampir sama dengan manusia; sebagian kisah menyebut mereka tidak punya lekukan di atas bibir (philtrum).
long_description.en: In Malaysian, Singaporean, Bruneian and Indonesian folklore, orang bunian are supernatural beings said to be unseen by most people except those with spiritual sight. The word is often rendered as elves, yet it literally means hidden people or whistling people. They are depicted as lovely, wearing old Southeast Asian dress and looking almost like humans; some accounts say they have no philtrum, the groove above the lip.

long_description.id: Orang bunian dikatakan tinggal di hutan lebat atau pegunungan tinggi di Sumatra, Kalimantan, dan Semenanjung Malaya, jauh dari manusia, tetapi juga di dekat permukiman, bahkan serumah dengan keluarga manusia. Masyarakat mereka mirip masyarakat Melayu kuno, dengan keluarga, klan, dan bangsawan, dan mereka harus ditenangkan dengan ritual tertentu sebelum manusia boleh memasuki wilayahnya.
long_description.en: Orang bunian are said to live in deep forests or high mountains of Sumatra, Borneo and the Malay Peninsula, far from people, but also near settlements, even sharing houses with human families. Their society resembles that of the ancient Malay world, with families, clans and royalty, and they must be appeased with rituals before humans may enter their land.

long_description.id: Mereka umumnya dianggap baik hati dan suka menolong manusia, terutama dukun, bomoh, dan pawang. Orang bunian dapat menikah dengan manusia dan melahirkan anak yang tak terlihat; dalam beberapa kisah, laki-laki yang pernah menikahi perempuan bunian kembali ke keluarganya dan mendapati bahwa bertahun-tahun telah berlalu dan semua orang yang dikenalnya sudah meninggal. Dalam salah satu kisah, sebagian anggota rombongan pergi ke kota pada malam hari dan kembali paginya dengan mengaku telah dibawa pergi ke sebuah kota bunian.
long_description.en: They are generally considered benevolent, befriending and helping humans, especially dukun, bomoh and pawang. Orang bunian can marry humans and bear invisible children; in some tales, men who married bunian women returned to their families to find that many years had passed and everyone they knew had died. One account tells of part of a group who walked into town after dark and returned at dawn claiming they had been whisked off to a bunian town.

long_description.id: Dalam teks klasik Melayu, "Orang Bunyian" disebut sebagai golongan roh yang sedikit sekali diketahui, tampak sebagai bangsa peri baik yang begitu polos sehingga mudah ditipu. Konon bila mereka sesekali masuk ke dusun untuk membeli sesuatu, mereka membayar tanpa menawar berapa pun harga yang diminta, dan di sebuah tempat bernama Jugra konon terdengar mereka mendayung perahu di sungai tanpa ada perahu yang tampak.
long_description.en: In the classic Malay text the "Orang Bunyian" are described as a class of spirits about whom very little is known, appearing as good fairies so simple-minded that they are easily cheated. When they occasionally come into a hamlet to buy something they are said to pay without bargaining whatever price is asked, and at a place called Jugra they were said to be heard paddling boats on the river with no boat in sight.

long_description.id: Kisah-kisah masa kini menggambarkan mereka sangat rupawan dan sering berbusana gaya Asia Tenggara kuno, serta dunia mereka mencerminkan dunia manusia, dengan keluarga, komunitas, pasar, dan bangsawan. Kisah bunian yang paling umum menyangkut disorientasi mendadak di tempat yang seharusnya dikenal, Penggambaran modern menambahkan ciri seperti peri, telinga runcing, dan busana ala fantasi.
long_description.en: Present-day accounts picture them as strikingly beautiful and often dressed in ancient Southeast Asian style, and picture their world as mirroring the human one, with families, communities, marketplaces and royalty. The most common bunian stories concern sudden disorientation in places that should be familiar. Modern depictions add elf-like features, pointed ears and fantasy-style attire.

claims.quote: In Malaysian, Singaporean, Bruneian and Indonesian folklore, Bunian people or Orang bunian ... are supernatural beings said to be invisible to most humans, except those with "spiritual sight".

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Malaysia, Singapura, Brunei, dan Indonesia, orang bunian adalah makhluk gaib yang konon tak terlihat oleh kebanyakan manusia, kecuali yang memiliki "penglihatan batin".
statement.en: In Malaysian, Singaporean, Bruneian and Indonesian folklore, orang bunian are supernatural beings said to be invisible to most humans, except those with "spiritual sight".

claims.quote: Orang bunian are described as beautiful, dressed in ancient Southeast Asian style, and nearly identical to humans in appearance. Some mythological accounts describe the lack of a philtrum. Modern depictions of Orang bunian deviate from the traditional folklore by including elf-like features, pointed ears, high fantasy-influenced attire, or modern Minangkabau long-coat clothing.

statement.id: Orang bunian digambarkan rupawan, berbusana gaya Asia Tenggara kuno, hampir sama dengan manusia, dan menurut sebagian cerita tak punya lekuk di atas bibir; penggambaran modern menambahkan ciri peri, telinga runcing, busana fantasi, atau mantel panjang Minangkabau.
statement.en: Orang bunian are beautiful, in ancient Southeast Asian dress, nearly identical to humans, some lacking a philtrum; modern depictions add elf-like features, pointed ears, fantasy attire or Minangkabau long coats.

claims.quote: Orang bunian are said to inhabit the deep forests or high mountains in Sumatra, Borneo & Malay Peninsula, far from human contact, as well as near human communities, and are even said to share the same houses as human families.

statement.id: Orang bunian dikatakan tinggal di hutan lebat atau pegunungan tinggi di Sumatra, Kalimantan, dan Semenanjung Malaya, juga di dekat permukiman, bahkan serumah dengan keluarga manusia.
statement.en: Orang bunian are said to live in deep forests or high mountains of Sumatra, Borneo and the Malay Peninsula, also near settlements, even sharing houses with human families.

claims.quote: According to legend, their social structure is similar to that of humans in the ancient Malay Peninsula, with families, clans, and royalty. As with other mythical beings in Indonesian folklore, Orang bunian often have supernatural powers, and must be appeased with certain rituals and customs before humans are allowed to trespass areas which they inhabit.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, struktur sosial mereka mirip masyarakat Melayu kuno di Semenanjung Malaya, dengan keluarga, klan, dan bangsawan; mereka punya kekuatan gaib dan harus ditenangkan dengan ritual sebelum manusia boleh memasuki wilayahnya.
statement.en: By legend their society resembles the ancient Malay Peninsula, with families, clans and royalty; they have supernatural powers and must be appeased with rituals before humans enter their land.

claims.quote: Orang bunian are generally regarded as benevolent, befriending and assisting humans, particularly magicians (dukun or bomoh) and shamans (pawang). They are said to be able to intermarry with humans, and bear invisible children.

statement.id: Orang bunian umumnya dianggap baik hati, berteman dan menolong manusia, terutama dukun, bomoh, dan pawang; mereka dapat menikah dengan manusia dan melahirkan anak yang tak terlihat.
statement.en: Orang bunian are generally benevolent, befriending and helping humans, especially dukun, bomoh and pawang; they can marry humans and bear invisible children.

claims.quote: However, after returning to human society, they found that many years had passed and everyone they once knew had died. These narratives have been compared to Urashima Taro and Rip Van Winkle.

statement.id: Laki-laki yang kembali dari masyarakat bunian mendapati bertahun-tahun telah berlalu dan semua kenalannya telah meninggal; kisah ini dibandingkan dengan Urashima Taro dan Rip Van Winkle.
statement.en: Men who returned from bunian society found many years had passed and everyone they knew had died; these tales are compared to Urashima Taro and Rip Van Winkle.

claims.quote: “A part of the group went to town at night. They came back in the morning saying they had been spirited away into a Bunian town.”

statement.id: Dalam satu kesaksian, sebagian rombongan pergi ke kota pada malam hari dan kembali pagi harinya mengaku telah dibawa ke kota bunian.
statement.en: In one account, part of a group went to town at night and returned in the morning saying they had been spirited away to a bunian town.

claims.quote: These narratives have been compared to Urashima Taro and Rip Van Winkle.

statement.id: Kisah-kisah ini dibandingkan dengan Urashima Taro dan Rip Van Winkle.
statement.en: These narratives are compared to Urashima Taro and Rip Van Winkle.

claims.quote: While the term is often translated as "elves", it literally translates to "hidden people" or "whistling people".

statement.id: Istilah ini sering diterjemahkan sebagai "peri" (elves), tetapi secara harfiah berarti "orang tersembunyi" atau "orang bersiul".
statement.en: The term is often translated as "elves", but literally translates to "hidden people" or "whistling people".

claims.quote: Some mythological accounts describe the lack of a philtrum.

statement.id: Sebagian kisah mitologis menggambarkan mereka tidak memiliki philtrum (lekukan di atas bibir).
statement.en: Some mythological accounts describe them as lacking a philtrum.

claims.quote: Modern depictions of Orang bunian deviate from the traditional folklore by including elf-like features, pointed ears, high fantasy-influenced attire, or modern Minangkabau long-coat clothing.

claims.quote: the "Orang Bunyian," a class of Malay spirits about whom very little seems known. The latter appear to be a race of good fairies, who are so simple-minded that they can be very easily cheated.

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik, "Orang Bunyian" disebut sebagai golongan roh Melayu yang sedikit sekali diketahui; mereka tampak sebagai bangsa peri baik yang begitu polos sehingga mudah ditipu.
statement.en: In the classic text, the "Orang Bunyian" are described as a class of Malay spirits about whom very little seems known; they appear to be a race of good fairies so simple-minded that they can be very easily cheated.

claims.quote: Thus it is always said of them, that whenever they come into a hamlet, as they may occasionally do, to buy anything, they always pay without bargaining whatever price is asked, however exorbitant it may be.

statement.id: Dikatakan bahwa bila sesekali masuk ke dusun untuk membeli sesuatu, mereka selalu membayar tanpa menawar berapa pun harga yang diminta, setinggi apa pun.
statement.en: It is said that whenever they occasionally come into a hamlet to buy anything, they always pay without bargaining whatever price is asked, however exorbitant.

claims.quote: I have been told of their existence at Kapar village (near Klang in Selangor), at Jugra, where it was said they might formerly be heard paddling their boats upon the river when no boat was visible, and elsewhere.

statement.id: Penulis diberi tahu tentang keberadaan mereka di desa Kapar (dekat Klang di Selangor) dan di Jugra, tempat konon dahulu terdengar mereka mendayung perahu di sungai ketika tak ada perahu yang tampak.
statement.en: The author was told of their existence at Kapar village (near Klang in Selangor) and at Jugra, where it was said they might formerly be heard paddling their boats on the river when no boat was visible.

claims.quote: They are described as strikingly beautiful, often dressed in the style of ancient Southeast Asia, as though they belong to a version of the region untouched by time.

statement.id: Mereka digambarkan sangat rupawan dan sering berbusana gaya Asia Tenggara kuno, seolah berasal dari versi kawasan itu yang tak tersentuh waktu.
statement.en: They are described as strikingly beautiful, often dressed in ancient Southeast Asian style, as though from a version of the region untouched by time.

claims.quote: In folklore, their world mirrors ours – families, communities, marketplaces, even royalty.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat, dunia mereka mencerminkan dunia kita: keluarga, komunitas, pasar, bahkan bangsawan.
statement.en: In folklore, their world mirrors ours: families, communities, marketplaces, even royalty.

claims.quote: A bomoh reportedly claimed assistance from Bunian beings during rituals, describing figures that appeared regal, elegant and distinctly human-like. “They said the Bunian came from Gunung Ledang and lived in a hidden city more advanced than ours.”

statement.id: Seorang bomoh dikabarkan mengaku dibantu makhluk bunian dalam ritual, menggambarkan sosok yang tampak agung, anggun, dan sangat mirip manusia; menurut penuturan itu, bunian berasal dari Gunung Ledang dan tinggal di kota tersembunyi yang lebih maju daripada kota kita.
statement.en: A bomoh reportedly claimed help from Bunian beings during rituals, describing figures that appeared regal, elegant and distinctly human-like; in the account, the Bunian came from Gunung Ledang and lived in a hidden city more advanced than ours.

claims.quote: Among the most common Bunian stories are those involving sudden disorientation in places that should be familiar.

statement.id: Di antara kisah bunian yang paling umum adalah kisah tentang disorientasi mendadak di tempat yang seharusnya dikenal.
statement.en: Among the most common Bunian stories are those about sudden disorientation in places that should be familiar.

claims.quote: Then, after turning back only moments later, the bamboo path was gone. Gone. No trace. No wrong turn. No obvious explanation.

statement.id: Dalam salah satu kisah, seorang pendaki melihat jalan setapak berpagar bambu yang indah, tetapi beberapa saat setelah berbalik, jalan itu lenyap tanpa jejak dan tanpa penjelasan.
statement.en: In one account a hiker saw a lovely bamboo-lined path, but moments after turning back the path was gone, with no trace and no obvious explanation.

short_description.id: Orang Mawas adalah kriptid dalam cerita rakyat Melayu yang konon menghuni hutan Johor dan Singapura, digambarkan tinggi 2,4–3 meter, berjalan dengan dua kaki, dan berbulu hitam.
short_description.en: The Orang Mawas is a cryptid of Malay folklore said to inhabit the jungles of Johor and Singapore, described as 2.4–3 m tall, bipedal and covered in black fur.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Melayu, Orang Mawas atau Mawas, yang juga disebut Orang Dalam, adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan menghuni hutan Johor, Malaysia, dan Singapura. Ia digambarkan setinggi sekitar 2,4–3 meter, berjalan dengan dua kaki, berbulu hitam, dan dilaporkan memakan ikan serta menjarah kebun buah.
long_description.en: In Malay folklore, the Orang Mawas or Mawas, also called the Orang Dalam, is a cryptid reported to inhabit the jungles of Johor, Malaysia, and Singapore. It is described as about 2.4–3 m tall, bipedal and covered in black fur, and has been reported eating fish and raiding orchards.

long_description.id: Orang Asli setempat menyebutnya hantu jarang gigi, yang berarti hantu bergigi jarang. Klaim penampakan mawas yang tercatat sudah ada sejak 1871. Sebagian orang menduga makhluk ini Gigantopithecus yang masih hidup atau ingatan rakyat tentang hewan itu, sedangkan kalangan ilmiah cenderung menganggap penampakan itu sebagai beruang madu yang salah dikenali.
long_description.en: The local Orang Asli call it hantu jarang gigi, meaning snaggle-toothed ghost. Claims of sightings have been on record since 1871. Some speculate it may be a surviving Gigantopithecus or a folk memory of one, while scientists generally write the sightings off as sun bears mistaken for something else.

long_description.id: Sebuah buku folklor Melayu mencatat tradisi tentang kera besar mirip manusia bernama Mawas, yang konon membuat tempat berlindung di cabang pohon, dilahirkan dengan bilah parang di lengan bawah, dan dipercaya kadang menculik serta kawin dengan manusia; penulisnya menganggapnya ingatan akan orang utan atau mias dari Kalimantan. Kamus Dewan mendefinisikan mawas sebagai monyet besar termasuk orang hutan dan cimpanzi, dan di Sumatra kata mawas atau maias adalah nama umum orang utan.
long_description.en: A Malay folklore book records a tradition of a great man-like ape called the Mawas, said to make shelters in the forks of trees, to be born with a woodknife blade in place of the forearm bone, and believed occasionally to carry off and mate with humans; its author takes it to be a reminiscence of the orang-outang or mias of Borneo. Kamus Dewan defines mawas as a large monkey including the orangutan and chimpanzee, and in Sumatra the word mawas or maias is a common name for the orangutan.

long_description.id: Pada awal 2006 laporan berita menyebut "demam Bigfoot" memenuhi judul surat kabar Malaysia, dengan penampakan makhluk berbulu mirip gorila di hutan Johor, dan Malaysia berencana mengirim dua tim ilmuwan. Seorang narasumber bernama Chow mengatakan penduduk asli telah melihatnya selama beberapa generasi dan legenda mereka menyebutnya hantu bergigi jarang. Penyelidik paranormal kemudian menjelajah Taman Nasional Endau-Rompin dan menemukan jejak yang menurut mereka menunjukkan tinggi tiga setengah meter; pemerintah Johor membentuk komite ilmuwan resmi dan mengimbau warga menganggap makhluk itu bagian dari warisan negara bagian.
long_description.en: In early 2006 news reports said "Bigfoot" fever dominated Malaysian newspaper headlines, with sightings of a hairy gorilla-like creature in Johor forests, and Malaysia planned to send two teams of scientists. Chow, quoted in a news report, said forest natives have known of it across generations and name it the snaggle-toothed ghost in their legends. Paranormal investigators later searched Endau-Rompin National Park and found a footprint they say indicates a height of three and a half metres; the Johor government formed an official committee of scientists and urged people to regard the creatures as part of the state's heritage.

claims.quote: "Bigfoot" fever has dominated Malaysian newspaper headlines for several weeks now, with several dramatic sightings of a hairy, gorilla-like creature reported in the thick forest in the southern state of Johor.

statement.id: Sebuah laporan berita menyatakan "demam Bigfoot" memenuhi judul surat kabar Malaysia selama beberapa pekan, dengan beberapa penampakan dramatis makhluk berbulu mirip gorila di hutan lebat negara bagian Johor.
statement.en: A news report says "Bigfoot" fever dominated Malaysian newspaper headlines for several weeks, with several dramatic sightings of a hairy, gorilla-like creature in the thick forest of the southern state of Johor.

claims.quote: One local man said he saw a 10-foot (three metre) tall ape standing on two legs beside a river, according to one report.

statement.id: Menurut satu laporan, seorang warga setempat mengaku melihat kera setinggi 10 kaki (tiga meter) berdiri dengan dua kaki di tepi sungai.
statement.en: According to one report, a local man said he saw a 10-foot (three metre) tall ape standing on two legs beside a river.

claims.quote: PlanetArk 30 Jan 06 Malaysia Scientists to Hunt "Bigfoot" in Rainforest KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysia plans to send two teams of scientists to scour its southern rainforests and track down a huge ape said to have been spotted there, a government official said on Friday.

statement.id: Dalam berita bertanggal 30 Jan 2006, Malaysia dilaporkan berencana mengirim dua tim ilmuwan menyisir hutan hujan selatannya untuk melacak kera raksasa yang dikabarkan terlihat di sana.
statement.en: In a news item dated 30 Jan 2006, Malaysia was reported to plan sending two teams of scientists to scour its southern rainforests to track down a huge ape said to have been spotted there.

claims.quote: Natives who live in the jungle have seen it for generations and their legends call it the 'snaggle-toothed ghost'," said Chow.

statement.id: Seorang narasumber bernama Chow mengatakan penduduk asli yang tinggal di hutan telah melihatnya selama beberapa generasi dan legenda mereka menyebutnya "hantu bergigi jarang".
statement.en: A person named Chow said natives who live in the jungle have seen it for generations and their legends call it the "snaggle-toothed ghost".

claims.quote: An entire Bigfoot colony is said to have moved there from the jungles of Perak in the North during the 70s. Also known as the tropical Yeti or Mawas, the huge creatures reportedly have dense growth of hair on several parts of their body.

statement.id: Dikabarkan seluruh koloni "Bigfoot" pindah ke sana dari hutan Perak di utara pada tahun 70-an; makhluk besar itu juga dikenal sebagai Yeti tropis atau Mawas dan konon berbulu lebat di beberapa bagian tubuhnya.
statement.en: An entire "Bigfoot" colony is said to have moved there from the jungles of Perak in the north in the 70s; the huge creatures, also known as the tropical Yeti or Mawas, reportedly have dense hair on several parts of their body.

claims.quote: The paranormal investigators from Singapore, USA and the UK were invited by their Malaysian counterparts, a group known as the "Uncle Seekers." At Endau-Rompin National Park in the state of Johor, they ventured deep into the forest with the help of local guides.

statement.id: Penyelidik paranormal dari Singapura, Amerika Serikat, dan Inggris yang diundang rekan Malaysia mereka menjelajah jauh ke dalam hutan Taman Nasional Endau-Rompin di Johor bersama pemandu setempat.
statement.en: Paranormal investigators from Singapore, the USA and the UK, invited by Malaysian counterparts, ventured deep into the forest at Endau-Rompin National Park in Johor with local guides.

claims.quote: The clearest footprint found by the team had a four-inch depth. Going by that, and the height of broken tree branches overhead, the investigators believe an adult Bigfoot can reach a height of three and a half metres, and weigh more than 200 kilogrammes!

statement.id: Tim penyelidik menyatakan jejak terjelas yang mereka temukan sedalam empat inci, dan dari jejak itu serta tinggi dahan patah mereka memperkirakan seekor dewasa setinggi tiga setengah meter dengan bobot lebih dari 200 kilogram.
statement.en: The investigators said the clearest footprint they found was four inches deep, and from it and the height of broken branches they believe an adult can reach three and a half metres and weigh over 200 kilograms.

claims.quote: The Johor government has formed an official committee of research scientists, and are urging Malaysians to consider the creatures as part of the state's heritage.

statement.id: Pemerintah Johor membentuk komite resmi ilmuwan peneliti dan mengimbau warga Malaysia menganggap makhluk itu bagian dari warisan negara bagian.
statement.en: The Johor government formed an official committee of research scientists and urged Malaysians to regard the creatures as part of the state's heritage.

short_description.id: Oshira-sama adalah dewa pelindung rumah dalam cerita rakyat Jepang, ditemukan di wilayah timur laut; wujudnya sepasang tongkat murbei berwajah kuda dan gadis.
short_description.en: Oshira-sama is a household guardian deity of Japanese folklore, found in the northeast and embodied as a pair of mulberry sticks bearing a horse's and a maiden's faces.

long_description.id: Oshira-sama adalah dewa pelindung rumah dalam cerita rakyat Jepang, ditemukan di seluruh wilayah timur laut Jepang. Ia umumnya dipandang sebagai pelindung pertanian dan produksi ulat sutra, tetapi belum ada kesepakatan tentang asal nama dan ciri khususnya. Sebagian kebiasaan rumah membatasi daging dan siapa yang boleh menyentuh wujud sucinya.
long_description.en: Oshira-sama is a guardian deity of the household in Japanese folklore, found across the northeast of Japan. It is commonly viewed as a tutelary of agriculture and silkworm production, but little agreement has been reached on the origin of its name and its specific characteristics. Some household customs restrict meat and who may touch its sacred image.

long_description.id: Gambarnya memadukan wajah kuda dan perempuan muda. Benda pemujaannya umumnya sepasang tongkat murbei sepanjang sekitar 30 cm dengan wajah laki-laki dan perempuan atau kepala kuda, yang dikenakan lapisan kain yang ditambah setiap tahun. Satu mitos menghubungkan dewa itu dengan cinta antara gadis dan kuda jantan: kulit kuda yang dibunuh ayah sang gadis membungkus putrinya dan membawanya ke langit, lalu keduanya turun sebagai ulat sutra dan menjadi dewa penjaga keluarga.
long_description.en: Its images combine the faces of a horse and a maiden. The object of worship is generally a pair of mulberry sticks roughly 30 cm in length, carved or painted with male and female faces or a horse's head, clothed in layers of cloth added each year. One myth connects the deity with love between a maiden and a stallion: the hide of the stallion killed by the maiden's father wrapped around his daughter and took her to heaven, and the two later descended as silkworms and became guardian gods of families.

long_description.id: Perempuan memegang peran sentral dalam pemujaan, dan hari rayanya (meinichi) jatuh pada hari keenam belas bulan pertama, ketiga, dan kesembilan kalender lunar. Itako memanggil kehadiran kami dengan mantra, menggerakkan boneka Oshira seperti menari (oshira asobase), dan meramal untuk desa atau rumah tangga. Pemujaan mengandung pantangan, dan bila tidak dipuja semestinya Oshirasama dapat menimpakan kutukan atau terbang pergi.
long_description.en: Women play the central roles in the cult, and its festival, meinichi, is held in the first, third and ninth months of the lunar calendar, on the sixteenth day. The itako invokes the kami's presence with a mantra, moves the Oshira dolls as if dancing (oshira asobase), and performs divinations for the village or households. The cult involves taboos, and if it is not worshipped properly Oshirasama may visit a curse or fly away.

cultural_context.id: Perempuan memegang peran sentral dalam pemujaan Oshirasama, dan itako memakai boneka Oshira dalam ritus pemanggilan dan ramalan untuk desa atau rumah tangga.
cultural_context.en: Women play the central roles in the cult of Oshirasama, and itako use the Oshira dolls in rites of invocation and in divination for villages or households.
